1. Scope and Purpose
====================

During production execution, costs are captured and compared with planned costs. Variances are analyzed to understand inefficiencies, resource bottlenecks, or material wastage. This real-time cost insight is essential for improving future production runs.

This document describes the PPC calculation and how the analysis of the calculated figures could be done. In addition the marking and release process of the checked PPC calculation is specified.

In the below process flow of the L3(V) process [Subsequent Planning - Product Cost - Costing Plan](https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/display/TRANS4M/Subsequent+Planning+-+Product+Cost+-+Costing+Plan), the yellow marked process steps contain the costing and analysis activities.

![](https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/download/attachments/embedded-page/TRANS4M2/PPC%20Serial%20Production%20-%20Costing%20and%20Analysis%20-%20User%20Documentation/image-2023-10-3_20-50-43.png?api=v2)

![](https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/download/attachments/embedded-page/TRANS4M2/PPC%20Serial%20Production%20-%20Costing%20and%20Analysis%20-%20User%20Documentation/image-2023-10-3_20-51-42.png?api=v2)

2. Process Description and Explanation
======================================

**PPC Calculation** refers to the calculation of production costs related to serial production. It involves determining the planned and actual costs of manufacturing products in a serial production environment.

The calculation includes all relevant cost categories like materials, labor, machine time and overhead.

After the creation of a PPC calculation (cost estimate) for a material, it must be **checked, marked, and released** to confirm the costing data is valid and can be used in production and accounting.

The PPC calculation could be done when the preconditions are fulfilled as:

* Availability of Material Master, Routings, BOM and Production Versions
* Maintained mixing ratios and lot size
* Purchase prices for external procured parts and subcontracting materials
* CKD info records
* Determination of overhead surcharges and cost center tariffs

Marking and releasing are important because it prevents use of incomplete or incorrect cost estimates in production and financial processes, locks the cost estimate so no unintended changes occur after approval and enables accurate cost postings and variance analysis based on the approved plan. Also it supports compliance, Tax and audit requirements.

Steps:

* Calculate or update the PPC cost estimate
* Display and review the cost estimate carefully
* Mark the cost estimate to flag it as internally checked
* Release the cost estimate to confirm approval
* Costing run can be run to perform the same steps (Calculate → Mark → Release) but for multiple materials in one run

1. Scope and Purpose
====================

During production execution, costs are captured and compared with planned costs. Variances are analyzed to understand inefficiencies, resource bottlenecks, or material wastage. This real-time cost insight is essential for improving future production runs.

This document describes the PPC calculation and how the analysis of the calculated figures could be done. In addition the marking and release process of the checked PPC calculation is specified.

In the below process flow of the L3(V) process [Subsequent Planning - Product Cost - Costing Plan](https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/display/TRANS4M/Subsequent+Planning+-+Product+Cost+-+Costing+Plan), the yellow marked process steps contain the costing and analysis activities.

![](https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/download/attachments/embedded-page/TRANS4M2/PPC%20Serial%20Production%20-%20Costing%20and%20Analysis%20-%20User%20Documentation/image-2023-10-3_20-50-43.png?api=v2)

![](https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/download/attachments/embedded-page/TRANS4M2/PPC%20Serial%20Production%20-%20Costing%20and%20Analysis%20-%20User%20Documentation/image-2023-10-3_20-51-42.png?api=v2)

2. Process Description and Explanation
======================================

**PPC Calculation** refers to the calculation of production costs related to serial production. It involves determining the planned and actual costs of manufacturing products in a serial production environment.

The calculation includes all relevant cost categories like materials, labor, machine time and overhead.

After the creation of a PPC calculation (cost estimate) for a material, it must be **checked, marked, and released** to confirm the costing data is valid and can be used in production and accounting.

The PPC calculation could be done when the preconditions are fulfilled as:

* Availability of Material Master, Routings, BOM and Production Versions
* Maintained mixing ratios and lot size
* Purchase prices for external procured parts and subcontracting materials
* CKD info records
* Determination of overhead surcharges and cost center tariffs

Marking and releasing are important because it prevents use of incomplete or incorrect cost estimates in production and financial processes, locks the cost estimate so no unintended changes occur after approval and enables accurate cost postings and variance analysis based on the approved plan. Also it supports compliance, Tax and audit requirements.

Steps:

* Calculate or update the PPC cost estimate
* Display and review the cost estimate carefully
* Mark the cost estimate to flag it as internally checked
* Release the cost estimate to confirm approval
* Costing run can be run to perform the same steps (Calculate → Mark → Release) but for multiple materials in one run

[B2P | B2P-06.020 Execute cost center planning | Advanced]
Execute Cost Center Planning User Documentation
This document provides a comprehensive guide for executing cost center planning in SAP, focusing on GUI transactions in both R/3 and S/4HANA systems. The process involves planning cost center activities, calculating cost center prices, and transferring plan data to S/4HANA for reporting. The document outlines the scope, purpose, process steps, and system interactions required for effective cost center planning. Key highlights include: 

1. **Scope and Purpose**: The document aims to guide users through the steps necessary for cost center planning in SAP. The process remains consistent between R/3 and S/4HANA, with plan data saved in COS* tables and transferred to the ACDOCP table in S/4HANA for reporting via FIORI Apps.

2. **Process Description**: Cost center planning calculates cost center prices iteratively and automatically, ensuring accurate cost allocation and PPC costing. Key steps include:
   - Determining plan activity output (quantity)
   - Budgeting at the cost center level
   - Primary and secondary cost planning
   - Planning activity input
   - Allocating costs (indirect activity allocation, assessment, distribution, periodic reposting)
   - Surcharging for social cost accruals
   - Splitting planned costs into activity types
   - Automatic price calculation

3. **System Interaction**: The document provides detailed instructions for using SAP transactions to execute cost center planning. Key transactions include:
   - **OKP1/OKP2**: Manage/display period locks for planning
   - **KP04**: Set planner profiles
   - **KP97/KP98**: Copy cost planning between versions or from actuals
   - **KP06/KP26/KP46**: Plan cost elements, activity types, and statistical key figures
   - **KSCx/KSUx/KSVx**: Plan indirect activity allocation, assessment, and distribution
   - **KSS4**: Split plan costs to activity types
   - **KSPI**: Calculate activity plan prices
   - **/RB4C/CO_PLTR_2_S4H**: Transfer cost planning data from ERP (COS*) to S/4HANA (ACDOCP)

4. **Key Planning Steps**:
   - **Manage Period Lock for Plan**: Open all periods for the planning year using transaction OKP1.
   - **Planning Versions and Categories**: Map plan versions (e.g., Version 0) to S/4HANA plan categories (e.g., YX_0).
   - **Planner Profiles**: Use profiles for manual or Excel-based planning (YXCENTRL or YXCNTR_E).
   - **Planning Layouts**: Use specific layouts (e.g., YX-ACTTYPE, YX-PRIMARY) for different planning steps.
   - **Plan Activity Type (Output)**: Use KP26 to determine quantitative output and activity types for cost centers.
   - **Plan Primary Costs**: Use KP06 with layout YX-PRIMARY to plan primary costs by cost center and activity type.
   - **Plan Activity Input (T=A)**: Use KP06 with layout YX-ACTINPUT for Target = Actual activity allocation.
   - **Plan Secondary Costs**: Use KP06 with layout YX-SECORDCOS for secondary order costs.
   - **Plan Statistical Key Figures**: Use KP46 with layout YX-STATKEY to plan non-monetary data.
   - **Indirect Activity Allocation**: Use KSCB to allocate activity quantities based on statistical key figures.
   - **Plan Assessment and Distribution**: Use KSUx and KSVx for cost allocation between cost centers.
   - **Periodic Reposting**: Use KSWB for reposting plan primary costs (e.g., social cost accruals).
   - **Plan Surcharging**: Use KSP4 to calculate surcharges for social cost accruals.
   - **Reconcile Activity Type Planning**: Use KPSI to adjust planned activity output and input.
   - **Split Plan Costs**: Use KSS4 to allocate activity-independent costs to activity types.
   - **Calculate Activity Plan Prices**: Use KSPI to calculate tariffs for activity types.
   - **Transfer Plan Data to S/4HANA**: Use /RB4C/CO_PLTR_2_S4H to copy plan data from COS* to ACDOCP for reporting.

5. **Special Considerations**:
   - Use switching structures for correct cost component allocation.
   - Plan social costs directly on internal orders to avoid additional reposting steps.
   - Ensure proper setup of planner profiles, layouts, and cycles for accurate planning and allocation.
   - Validate and reconcile planned data before finalizing price calculations.

This document serves as a detailed reference for users to execute cost center planning effectively, ensuring accurate cost allocation and compliance with organizational requirements.

Enhancements in the subcontracting process from SAP ERP release 4.0 logic to 4.5 logic in S/4HANA.
A BOM (Bill of Materials) is needed to list the components which should be sent to the supplier.
A production version with a reference to the BOM is required. A reference to routing is not necessary.
An MRP area for each subcontractor must be created, with specific planning parameters (such as MRP type, lot sizing, procurement type) selectable for materials at the subcontracting MRP area level.
Default planning parameters are used if MRP area-specific material master records do not exist.
Separates subcontracting demand and stock into single subcontracting planning segments. Uncovered subcontracting demand is planned together with internal demand in the make-to-stock planning segment.
Plans the demand for each subcontractor separately using subcontracting MRP areas (available from SAP ERP release 4.5 logic).
Links provided to the Purchasing Subcontracting Process in S4.

1. Select the planning area, specifically "Order: Costs" and "Orders: Cost element/activity inputs."
2. Copy plan data from the ERP system (R3) Version 0 into S/4HANA under plan category YX_0 with Ledger 0L, ensuring amounts are in object currency (0).

4. Initially, execute the program in test mode to check for errors.
5. If the test run is successful, proceed to execute the program in normal mode to complete the transfer.

This process ensures that planned costs are accurately reflected in the S/4HANA ACDOCP table for reporting via FIORI Apps.

3.13. Plan Assessment between Cost Centers
------------------------------------------

Plan assessment between cost centers can be used for internal cost allocation in Regional Organizations or for Division/SG&A entities. In a production plant, assessment between cost centers is not allowed. Reason is, that the transfer of the fix/variable split from sender to receiver is not given because assessments are always defined fix.

Assessment between cost centers allocates plan costs from sender to receiver using secondary cost element. The original cost elements are assigned cumulatively, or in groups, to secondary cost elements. The original cost elements are not visible on the sender/receiver or in the allocation document.

This method of allocation can be used when original cost elements are not important for the receiver and allocation based on activity is not a requirement for other process area.

The key trigger points and posting logic for SG&A and MOH surcharges are as follows:

1. **Trigger Points**:
   - **Goods Receipt PO**: Initiates the surcharge process.
   - **Invoice Receipt Posting**: Triggered for price variances.
   - **Sales Order Settlement**: SG&A surcharge is posted during this process.

2. **Posting Logic**:
   - **SG&A Surcharge**:
     - Posted to the assigned Cost Center.
     - Offset posted to the Profitability Segment.
     - Involves internal order settlement and billing (KDN) for transfer to accounting.
   - **MOH Surcharge**:
     - Posted during goods issue based on Cost of Goods Sold (COGS).
     - MOH value is posted to the assigned Cost Center with an offset to the Profitability Segment.
     - Similar to SG&A, it involves internal order settlement and billing processes.

Both surcharges are part of the overhead surcharge process at the Distribution Center (DC) and are essential for accurate financial reporting and profitability analysis.

The DC CO-P&L with fix/var report includes the following key features and functionalities:

1. **Profit & Loss Structure**: Displays a complete P&L structure including Revenues, Cost of Sales (COS), Plan SG&A, PPC deviations, SG&A deviations, Other Operating Income and Expenses (OOIE), Gross Margin (GM1, GM3, GM4), and EBIT.

2. **Fix/Variable Concept**: Correct figures are shown only when the fix/variable concept is applied, allowing differentiation between fixed and variable costs.

3. **Data Source**: Based on financial statement version 1VS1 and restricted to object type 'EO' (COPA), enabling EBIT analysis only after month-end closure.

5. **Implementation**: Available as a separate FIORI app and accessible via Analysis for Office, created using WebDynpro technology.

6. **User Interaction**: Users can enter selection criteria (e.g., Company Code, Fiscal Year, Profit Center Hierarchy) and drill down to detailed levels of single G/L accounts and document numbers.

7. **Currency Display**: Values are displayed in the company code currency (e.g., PLN for DCPL).

8. **Background Filter**: Uses Ledger 0L for filtering data.

9. **Profit Center Hierarchy**: Requires a profit center hierarchy for report execution, with specific hierarchies like DC_PSTD and DC_LSTD.

10. **User Variants**: Users can save local variants for quicker access in future sessions.

question: What is the difference between an S-BOM and a P-BOM?
golden_answer: An S-BOM (Selection Bill of Material) includes only components approved by the product development team for manufacturing and is applicable across all plants. A P-BOM (Plant Specific Bill of Material) is derived from the S-BOM and contains specific materials tailored to one plant, ensuring only relevant components are used for that plant.

question: What are the steps to create an S-BOM and distribute it within the SAP system?
golden_answer: To create an S-BOM, go to the PDM-Cockpit and select BOM (/RBR1/G_CA_UI_PDM). Enter the material number in the Material field or search using matchcode, then fill out the components with mandatory fields like Material number and Quantity. To distribute the S-BOM, select the Work Basket S-BOM, process the item, refresh the status to 'S-BOM Distributed,' and switch to the P-BOM Work Basket for further actions.

question: How would you apply the process of creating a P-BOM for a specific plant using components from an S-BOM?
golden_answer: To create a P-BOM, go to the Work Basket P-BOM and select 'Edit P-BOM.' Choose the required components from the S-BOM and transfer them to the P-BOM. Verify and save the changes, then complete the process by refreshing the P-BOM Work Basket to confirm the status has changed to 'P-BOM completed.'

question: What is the difference between an S-BOM and a P-BOM?
golden_answer: An S-BOM (Selection Bill of Material) includes only components approved by the responsible product development team and is used for manufacturing across all plants. A P-BOM (Plant-Specific Bill of Material) contains specific materials tailored for one plant, derived from the S-BOM components, and is managed by PDM BOM roles.

question: What is the difference between an S-BOM and a P-BOM in the C2P process?
golden_source: C2P-04.040 Create & Change S-BOM, easy P-BOM.pptx
golden_answer: An S-BOM (Selection Bill of Materials) is a centralized source that includes only BOM components approved by the product development team and is required for manufacturing across all plants. A P-BOM (Plant-Specific Bill of Materials), on the other hand, is tailored for individual plant requirements and includes specific materials derived from the S-BOM for use in a particular plant.

question: What are the steps to create and distribute an S-BOM using the PDM-Cockpit?
golden_source: C2P-04.040 Create & Change S-BOM, easy P-BOM.pptx
golden_answer: To create and distribute an S-BOM using the PDM-Cockpit, first navigate to the PDM-Cockpit and select BOM (/RBR1/G_CA_UI_PDM). Enter the material number or search using matchcode, and fill in the required fields with components and quantities. Set the BOM status to 40 in the Header section and save. Then, go to the Work Basket S-BOM, select the material number, and start the distribution process by clicking on the 'Process' column. Finally, refresh the Work Basket to confirm the S-BOM status has changed to 'S-BOM finished'.

To create and distribute an S-BOM using the PDM-Cockpit, follow these steps:

### Create S-BOM:
1. **Access PDM-Cockpit**: Go to the PDM-Cockpit and select BOM (/RBR1/G_CA_UI_PDM).
2. **Enter Material Number**: Input the material number of the S-BOM in the Material field or search using matchcode.
3. **Fill Required Fields**: Complete the mandatory fields:
   - Material number (can also be searched by matchcode)
   - Quantity
4. **Specify Components**: Fill out the components with the following ICT categories:
   - Material (ICT = L)
   - Document (ICT = D)
   - Text (ICT = T)
5. **Structure for Entrance**: Navigate through the structure: BOM -> Selection group BOM (SBOM) -> SBOM Create.

### Distribute S-BOM:
1. **Access Work Basket**: Go to PDM-Cockpit and select Work Basket S-BOM.
2. **Select Material Number**: Enter the material number and press Enter.
3. **Process Selection**: Click on the Process in the column labeled 'Open' on the item highlighted with a yellow ellipse.
4. **Check BOM Status**: If the BOM Status is >=40, proceed with Step 2; otherwise, go directly to Step 3.
5. **Finalize Distribution**: Follow additional instructions in Step 3 titled 'Distribute S-BOM' to complete the distribution process. 

These steps will guide you through the creation and distribution of an S-BOM effectively.

question: What is the purpose of the Approval Framework (AFW) in sales order processing?
golden_answer: The Approval Framework (AFW) in sales order processing is an automatic function that monitors manual changes or specific process criteria, such as price changes or payment terms, and temporarily blocks further processing (e.g., delivery or invoice creation) until the changes are approved by an authorized user.

Then, input customer and material details, specify the validity period, check the net value and conditions, review the incompletion log, and save the quotation.

1. Scope and Purpose
====================

The PPC calculation for serial production in plants requires well defined master data in SAP system.

This document describes the required master data and to be checked data content which is needed to ensure accurate PCC calculation.

In the below process flow of the L3(V) process [Subsequent Planning - Product Cost - Costing Plan](https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=3888758559), the yellow marked process steps contain the check of required data.

![](https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/download/attachments/embedded-page/TRANS4M2/PPC%20Serial%20Production%20-%20Check%20Required%20Data%20-%20User%20Documentation/image-2023-9-12_21-49-31.png?api=v2)

![](https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/download/attachments/embedded-page/TRANS4M2/PPC%20Serial%20Production%20-%20Check%20Required%20Data%20-%20User%20Documentation/image-2023-9-12_20-34-40.png?api=v2)

2. Process Description and Explanation
======================================

The attached table provides an overview of the required master data and the to be checked data content:

| Master Data | Content | Transaction Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Material Master | The following views and fields in material master has to be maintained correctly:  |  |  | | --- | --- | | Basic Data 1 | * Cross plant material status * Base unit | | MRP2 | * Procurement type * Special procurement       e.g. Subcontracting: Procurement type "F" and       Special procurement "30" | | Accounting 1 | * Valuation class - more details could be find in the [link](https://inside-docupedia.bosch.com/confluence/display/TRANS4M/Process+Setting+for+Inventory+Accounting+Data+-+Process+Expert+Documentation) * S-price * Price unit * Price control * ML act. * Price determination | | Costing 1 | * Plant specific material status * Do not cost * With qty structure * Material origin * Origin group * Overhead group * Variance key * Production version * Costing lot size * SpecProcurement Costing | | Costing 2 | * Planned price 1 * Planned price date 1 |    To run the costing the cross plant and the plant specific material status must have a status "valid for costing" (e.g. 10, 40). | MM03 |
| Bill Of Material (BOM) | To create a valid PPC calculation the BOM has to be maintained for complete part list.     **Prerequisite for BOM:**   * Only BOM with defined usage (see screenshot) can be used for costing * BOM status must be valid for costing | CS03 |
| Routing | For inhouse produced parts valid routings have to be maintained.  The routing is used based on attached status hierarchy:  An operation should be costed if it is consuming either labor or machine times of a cost center.  If an operation should be costed both fields “CostingRelevancy” (operation) and field “Cost“ (control key) need to be ticked. | CA03 |
| Production Version | For PPC calculation and preliminary costing of PCC valid production versions have to be maintained for all inhouse materials in final and sub assembly.  Minimum requirements:   * production version not locked * valid * lot size 1 between 99.999.999 | C223 |
| Prices for external procured materials | The prices have to be maintained in Costing tab - field "Planned price 1". | MM03 |
| Cost Center Tariffs | Cost center tariffs for cost centers used in to be calculated operations (work centers) have to be provided for required activity types | KSBT |

This presentation by Bosch Rexroth, titled 'Information to Order (I2O),' provides a comprehensive overview of master data and its interdependencies within the I2O process. The slides cover various aspects of master data, including Customer Master Data, Material Master Data, Price Master, Output Master, and Material Determination, emphasizing their roles in ensuring efficient and error-free business transactions. 2. **Material Master Data**: Serves as the central source for material-related data, including material type, division, and pricing group. Relevant views (Basic Data, Sales Org Data) and transactions (MM01, MM02) are outlined.

3. **Price Master**: Manages pricing, discounts, and surcharges through condition records, access sequences, and pricing procedures. Key condition types (e.g., ZGLP, ZDBA) and their SAP tables (e.g., A118, A602) are detailed.

4. **Output Master**: Controls how documents (e.g., invoices, order confirmations) are communicated via mediums like print, email, or EDI. Key transactions (NACE, VV11) and tables (NAST, TNAPR) are provided.

5. **Material Determination**: Facilitates material substitution for various reasons, such as promotions or availability. Key transactions (VB11, VB12) and tables (KONH, KONP) are included.

6. **Master Data Interdependencies**: Explores the relationships between Customer Master Data, Material Master Data, and Organizational Data in creating sales orders and quotations. It highlights the role of pricing, output determination, and material validation in the I2O process.

Invest to Produce (I2P) Training Program Overview
The 'Invest to Produce (I2P) – Key User Training' program, presented by Bosch Rexroth AG under the 'Grownfield' initiative, focuses on the strategic alignment of investments with production goals through the SAP Project System (PS) module. The training emphasizes the integration of People, Technology, and Processes to enhance operational efficiency and compliance with CD 02200-005 requirements. The transition from Internal Orders to SAP PS enables the use of Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) elements for managing long-term, complex projects, improving resource planning, cost control, and financial management.

Key topics covered include:

1. **Introduction to I2P**: Overview of the I2P framework, which focuses on investing resources to enable effective procurement and production processes. The process includes budget allocation, asset capitalization, and the categorization of assets into external procurement and internal production.

2. **Roles and Responsibilities**: Explanation of Role-Based Access Control in SAP, with specific roles for project planners and process experts. Roles are requested through the OneIDM system and are country-specific.

3. **Project Lifecycle and Execution Process Flow**: The I2P lifecycle is divided into four phases:
   - **Initiation & Planning**: Create project definition, WBS, and allocate budgets.
   - **Execution Planning**: Create account assignments, schedules, and network activities.
   - **Procurement**: Execute procurement processes via MyBuy and perform technical closure.
   - **Closure**: Execute settlement runs and close projects.

4. **Step-by-Step Processes**: Detailed instructions for creating project definitions, WBS elements, and category-specific WBS elements (ME, TO, SW, OH, MR, TR). The training includes practical exercises for participants to apply these concepts.

6. **Project Types and Cost Settlements**: Explanation of various project types (e.g., ME, TO, SW, OH, MR, TR) and their respective cost settlement approaches, such as Asset under Construction (AuC) or direct settlement to fixed assets or cost centers.

Project Types and Cost Settlements for Investment Projects
This slide explains the categorization of different project types and their respective cost settlement approaches during the creation of the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS). It focuses on ensuring accurate planning, organization, and management of tasks within investment projects.
ME
ME-MAE inhouse produced or external procured
New investments as Machines, Assets, and Equipment with no value dependency. Procurement happens externally through suppliers or internally. Settled to Asset under Construction (AuC) and after technical closure, moved to fixed asset.
Asset under Construction (AuC)
TO
TO-Tools inhouse produced or external procured
New tools procured externally or produced internally and settled to AuC as per investment profile. Upon technical closure, it is moved to fixed asset.
Asset under Construction (AuC)
SW
SW-Software
New software procured externally and directly settled to fixed asset without AuC.
Fixed Asset, no AuC
OH
OH-Overhead Costs
Operating expenses related to investment, settled periodically to the Cost Center (PER) with a single account.
Cost Center
MR
MR-MAE re-used machines
Investments in re-used machines and equipment procured externally. Initially settled to AuC, moved to fixed asset after technical closure. Not linked to Bosch investment app as re-used machines are not part of CAPEX.
Asset under Construction (AuC)
TR
TR-Re-used tools
Investments in re-used tools procured externally. Initially settled to AuC, moved to fixed asset after technical closure. Not linked to Bosch investment app as re-used tools are not part of CAPEX.

question: What are the steps involved in the Purchasing and Transfer to R3 process?
golden_answer: The steps involved in the Purchasing and Transfer to R3 process are: 1) CU creates a delivery-relevant Sales Order (SO) with item category YVCP/YVCS, 2) Purchase Requisition (PR) is triggered, 3) Purchase Order (PO) with KNTTP=M is created, 4) SO is triggered in the R/3 plant with item categories XTAX or YZGS, 5) CU receives inbound delivery (case a) and posts Goods Receipt (GR), or receives an email (case b) and manually creates the inbound delivery and posts GR. Customization is required to exclude certificate items from Extended Warehouse Management (EWM).

The steps involved in the Purchasing and Transfer to R3 process are as follows:

1. CU creates a Sales Order (SO) which is delivery relevant, with item categories YVCP/YVCS.
2. A Purchase Requisition (PR) is triggered.

5. **Material Determination**: Facilitates material substitution for various reasons, such as promotions or availability. Key transactions (VB11, VB12) and tables (KONH, KONP) are included.

6. **Master Data Interdependencies**: Explores the relationships between Customer Master Data, Material Master Data, and Organizational Data in creating sales orders and quotations. It highlights the role of pricing, output determination, and material validation in the I2O process.

question: Can you summarize the process of certificate handling, from maintenance to billing, in the Order to Cash framework?
golden_answer: Certificates are maintained in sales documents as either sub-items of related materials (standard case) or as single main items (exception case). They are relevant for delivery but not printed on delivery notes, not processed in EWM, and require ATP checks during delivery creation. Certificates are billing-relevant and must be released via VF01 or batch job. They can also be archived in Vendor Sales Order and Country Unit Sales Order archives.

generated_answer:
The certificate handling process within the Order to Cash (O2C) framework involves several key steps:

1. **Sales Order Creation**: The Customer Unit (CU) creates a Sales Order (SO) that is delivery relevant, using specific item categories (YVCP/YVCS).

2. **Purchase Requisition Trigger**: Upon SO creation, a Purchase Requisition (PR) is automatically triggered.

3. **Purchase Order Creation**: A Purchase Order (PO) is generated with specific settings (KNTTP=M), indicating that it is goods receipt (GR) valuated and invoice relevant.

4. **Sales Order Processing in R/3**: The SO is processed in the R/3 plant, where it may involve different item categories, such as XTAX (outbound delivery without goods movement) or YZGS (no delivery).

5. **Inbound Delivery Management**: The CU receives an inbound delivery for case a (XTAX) and posts the Goods Receipt (GR). For case b (YZGS), the CU manually creates the inbound delivery based on an email notification and posts the GR.

6. **Certificate Item Management**: Certificate items are maintained as sub-items of related materials and are kept out of Extended Warehouse Management (EWM), meaning no picking or packing is required.

7. **Billing Relevance**: The items related to certificates are billing relevant and must be released using SAP transactions (e.g., VF01) for billing processes.

This structured approach ensures that certificates are effectively managed from creation through to billing, integrating various roles and processes within the O2C framework.

question: What is the purpose of the 'complete delivery' field in the Order to Cash process?
golden_answer: The 'complete delivery' field ensures that an order is delivered in its entirety. It adjusts all confirmed item-level dates to match the last confirmed delivery date and can be set manually or via an ORDERS Idoc.

Delivery Elements: Delivery Groups
Definition
A combination of items that should be delivered together.
Functionality
Delivery groups are used by the system to check availability of items that should be delivered together.
The delivery date of the latest schedule line within the delivery group is set as the general delivery date for the group.
Operation
During sales order processing, a number (up to three digits) can be entered to identify each delivery group, and this number is freely definable.
The system adjusts pre-existing requirements and changes material availability dates for individual items to match the determined delivery date for the group.
Benefits
Using delivery groups can reduce the number of deliveries.
Precondition
Items in a delivery group must share the same shipping point.
Exceptions
Delivery groups are automatically created for main and sub-items during SET/KIT-processing.

These changes reflect a modernization and operational adjustment in the transition from R/3 to S/4.

[O2C | O2C-02.012 Sales Order Standard with Down-Payment | Advanced]
Introduction: 2.5) Main Topics | Hints
DownPayment solution in S/4 is a Rexroth-wide solution in combination with the horizontal layer (PHL-system). The solution differs significantly from the solutions available in R/3. Since SAP plans to enhance only the 'billing plan' solution in the future, and not the 'condition-based solution', Bosch has decided to implement a solution incorporating the billing plan in S/4.
A customer places a sales order for high-value goods. Before delivery, the company requires a down payment to secure the order. In SAP, a DownPayment Request is created based on the billing plan in the sales order. Once the customer pays, the incoming payment clears the DownPayment Request and the DownPayment Invoice is created automatically. question: What are the key differences between managing free-of-charge sales orders in SAP R/3 and SAP S/4?
golden_source: O2C-02.021 Sales Order FOC with transfer of ownership.pptx
golden_answer: In SAP R/3, free-of-charge (FOC) items could be entered within the standard sales order, order reasons had no influence on tax determination, and goods could be sent to internal business partners. In SAP S/4, FOC items must use a separate order type (YVI1), order reasons influence tax determination, and it is not allowed to send FOC goods to internal business partners.

question: What are the steps involved in creating a Free of Charge subsequent delivery in SAP S/4 without transfer of ownership?

golden_answer: The steps are: 1) Start order creation using transaction VA01. 2) Select order type YVI2 and maintain organizational data with reference to the predecessor document. 3) Maintain header data by entering customer reference and date. 4) Select the specific order reason (e.g., Y70). 5) Check material and quantity, which are prefilled. 6) Verify pricing data with a 100% discount. 7) Enter the internal order number in the account assignment tab. 8) Save the order and initiate the approval framework.

question: What are the steps to create a free-of-charge sales order with NSGS material in SAP S/4?
golden_source: O2C-02.024 Sales Order FOC NSGS material without transfer of ownership.pptx
golden_answer: The steps to create a free-of-charge sales order with NSGS material in SAP S/4 are: 1) Start the sales order creation using transaction VA01, 2) Enter organizational data and select the order type YVI1, 3) Select 'without reference', 4) Enter the sold-to/ship-to party, customer reference, and order reason, 5) Enter the NSGS material number and item category YVF6, 6) Execute pricing data, 7) Enter the profit center and commodity group, and 8) Save the order.

Comprehensive Guide to Make-to-Stock (MTS) Production and SAP Production Order Management
This document provides a detailed overview of the Make-to-Stock (MTS) production strategy and SAP production order management processes, focusing on efficient manufacturing and supply chain operations. The MTS strategy, implemented under Bosch Rexroth AG's 'Produce to Supply' framework, emphasizes manufacturing based on demand forecasts rather than specific customer orders, enabling immediate delivery and short lead times. Key benefits include high product availability, economies of scale, efficient capacity utilization, and standardized processes. The process is triggered by Planned Independent Requirements (PIRs) and Material Requirements Planning (MRP), which generate Planned Orders for production.

The guide outlines the MTS process flow, including demand forecasting, planned order creation, production order conversion, production start, goods receipt posting, and delivery. It provides step-by-step instructions for converting planned orders to production orders, sequencing and releasing production orders, performing confirmations, and posting goods receipts. Technical advantages include seamless integration of MRP and Production Planning (PP), automated order generation, real-time cost visibility, and flexible stock management.

Additionally, the document details SAP production order management, covering the lifecycle from release to completion. Key steps include:
1. Releasing production orders via MD04 or COHV, with material availability checks and handling missing parts.
2. Printing production orders automatically or manually via CO02 and CO04N.
3. Creating warehouse requests and ensuring material supply for production.
4. Confirming operations via CO11N, with statuses updated to 'PCNF' (Partially Confirmed) or 'CNF' (Confirmed).
5. Posting goods receipts to anonymous stock for immediate fulfillment, updating the production order status to 'DLV' (Delivered).

System statuses track the production order lifecycle: CRTD → REL → PRT → GMPS → PCNF → CNF → DLV. Costs are collected on production orders to determine accurate manufacturing costs. The guide emphasizes the importance of stock availability, rapid delivery, and streamlined processes, supported by diagrams, SAP interface screenshots, and branding elements. This comprehensive reference ensures efficient implementation of MTS production and SAP production order management strategies.

Embargo Check
Country-specific sanctions (embargoes) are imposed by authorities specifying trade restrictions against certain nations.
Legal Control Check of Items Subject to Export Control
Authorities aim to prevent the proliferation of military and dual-use items by issuing Lists of Goods with export restrictions. These items require specific authorization for export.

   - Blocked sales documents due to export control checks prevent subsequent process steps, including delivery, picking, and packing.

Guide to Packing Goods for Outbound Shipping in SAP EWM
This guide provides an overview of the process for packing goods for outbound shipping using SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM). The process begins by accessing the transaction `scwm.pack` and selecting the warehouse number and outbound delivery order in the warehouse request field. The packer typically receives a picking list and manually checks for any order-related packing information, as there are no automatic flags or pop-ups for such details. Delivery items are packed into shipping handling units (HUs) by selecting the material, choosing appropriate packaging material, and using drag-and-drop functionality. If an item does not fit into the current handling unit, it must be split, and a new handling unit is created. The system can automatically pre-fill the new handling unit, and the packer can adjust the weight, volume, and dimensions as needed. Once packed, the handling unit label is printed, and the process is finalized in the packing monitor. This triggers background activities such as determining the forwarder, updating the ERP outbound delivery, and preparing the goods for physical movement to the staging area. The process may vary depending on the warehouse structure and organization.

Guide to Packing Goods for Outbound Shipping in SAP EWM
This guide provides an overview of the process for packing goods for outbound shipping using SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM). The process begins by accessing the transaction `scwm.pack` and selecting the warehouse number and outbound delivery order in the warehouse request field. The packer typically receives a picking list and manually checks for any order-related packing information, as there are no automatic flags or pop-ups for such details. Delivery items are packed into shipping handling units (HUs) by selecting the material, choosing appropriate packaging material, and using drag-and-drop functionality. If an item does not fit into the current handling unit, it must be split, and a new handling unit is created. The system can automatically pre-fill the new handling unit, and the packer can adjust the weight, volume, and dimensions as needed. Once packed, the handling unit label is printed, and the process is finalized in the packing monitor. This triggers background activities such as determining the forwarder, updating the ERP outbound delivery, and preparing the goods for physical movement to the staging area. The process may vary depending on the warehouse structure and organization.

The key steps involved in the SAP S/4 Package Goods Process with a focus on certificates include:

1. **Sales Order Creation**: The Customer Unit (CU) creates a delivery-relevant Sales Order (SO) with specific item categories (YVCP/YVCS).

7. **Certificate Process**: The process for certificates follows the same steps as for the Customer Service Process (CSP). If the SO from the R/3 plant does not include an outbound delivery, the CU will manually create the inbound delivery.

8. **Triggering Subsequent Steps**: The CU's inbound delivery triggers all subsequent steps in the sales area on the CU side.

These steps ensure efficient handling of package goods and compliance with certificate requirements within the Order to Cash process.

Delivery items are packed into shipping handling units (HUs) by selecting the material, choosing appropriate packaging material, and using drag-and-drop functionality. If an item does not fit into the current handling unit, it must be split, and a new handling unit is created. The system can automatically pre-fill the new handling unit, and the packer can adjust the weight, volume, and dimensions as needed. Once packed, the handling unit label is printed, and the process is finalized in the packing monitor. This triggers background activities such as determining the forwarder, updating the ERP outbound delivery, and preparing the goods for physical movement to the staging area. The process may vary depending on the warehouse structure and organization.

question: What steps should be taken if the forwarder needs to be updated after packing?
golden_source: O2C-03.032 Assign Freight Forwarder - manually (Material Weight).pptx
golden_answer: If the forwarder needs to be updated after packing, the update must be done manually, and the forwarder label printout must be repeated. This process involves additional effort and increases the risk of using incorrect outputs.

question: Can you summarize the prerequisites and key steps for manually assigning a freight forwarder based on material weight?
golden_source: O2C-03.032 Assign Freight Forwarder - manually (Material Weight).pptx
golden_answer: Prerequisites include having a forwarding agent as a business partner with role CMD10, no linkage between BP forwarder and BP customer, and an outbound delivery that is created but not completely packed. Key steps are entering the change mode of the Outbound Delivery Order (ODO) in transaction /SCWM/PRDO, changing the indicator to 'M', manually changing the freight forwarder in the 'Partner' field, confirming the log, and verifying the changes in the ERP outbound delivery system.

question: Why is it important to carefully consider changing the indicator to 'M' before packing in the manual freight forwarder assignment process?
golden_source: O2C-03.034 Assign Freight Forwarder - manually (HU weight).pptx
golden_answer: Changing the indicator to 'M' is irreversible, and the result will not be overwritten by the LSP Determination Table after packing. If changes are needed after packing, the forwarder must be manually adjusted, which involves additional effort and increases the risk of using incorrect outputs, such as forwarder labels.

question: What are the steps to manually assign a freight forwarder based on handling unit (HU) weight?

golden_answer: 1. Enter change mode of the outbound delivery via transaction /SCWM/FD, search for the OD number, and select the respective line to edit. 2. Change the indicator in the 'Partner' tab to 'M' using the dialogue button. 3. Manually change the forwarder in the 'Partner' field or using the dialogue button. 4. Confirm the log and proceed by clicking 'Continue' or pressing Enter. 5. If needed, change the forwarder service level using transaction /SCWM/MON. 6. Check the ERP Outbound Delivery in SAP (Transaction VL03n) to ensure updates are reflected.

The steps involved in determining the carrier during the creation of an Outbound Delivery Order (ODO) in the EWM system are as follows:

1. **Creation of ODO**: The carrier determination process begins when the ODO is created in the EWM system.

2. **Parameter Evaluation**: The system evaluates predefined rules based on parameters such as weight, shipping type, Incoterms, and shipping conditions.

3. **Initial Determination**: An initial carrier is determined based on the parameters available at the time of ODO creation.

4. **Weight Check**: If the delivery weight exceeds a certain threshold (e.g., 30 kg), the system may change the carrier based on the updated weight after packaging.

5. **Final Determination**: After packaging is completed and the final weight of all handling units (HUs) is available, the carrier determination may be updated.

6. **Update in ERP**: The determined carrier information is then updated in the ERP delivery.

7. **Review and Analysis**: The determination can be analyzed using the BRF+ transaction and the determination table to ensure the correct carrier is selected based on matching parameters.

This content provides an overview of the process for determining carriers and logistics service providers (LSP) in SAP S/4HANA, specifically focusing on the integration between ERP and EWM systems. Overview of Carrier and LSP Determination in SAP S/4HANA
This content provides an overview of the process for determining carriers and logistics service providers (LSP) in SAP S/4HANA, specifically focusing on the integration between ERP and EWM systems. The carrier or forwarding agent is not visible in the sales order but is determined during the creation of the outbound delivery order (ODO) in EWM. question: What are the steps to create a new Transportation Unit (TU) in the SAP S/4 system?
golden_answer: To create a new Transportation Unit (TU) in SAP S/4: 1) Press the 'Create' button. 2) Optionally select a Carrier. 3) Add Means of Transport (e.g., dummy value YVT1). 4) Add Packaging Material (e.g., dummy value 6001006101). 5) Specify Activity Direction as '2 Outbound'. 6) Confirm by pressing 'Continue' or ENTER. 7) Press the 'Save' button. TU-related information can be adjusted before saving.

question: How does the transition from SAP R/3 to SAP S/4 impact the export declaration status and transport blocking?
golden_answer: In SAP R/3, the export declaration status was available to show if an export declaration was already requested, whereas in SAP S/4, this status is not available and is instead managed by adding free text in the Transportation Unit (TU). For transport blocking, SAP R/3 allowed transport to be blocked for loading until the transport block was released, while in SAP S/4, TUs can be blocked, but the blocking status is not available in the EWM overview.

question: What are the steps to create a new Transportation Unit (TU) in the SAP system?
golden_answer: To create a new Transportation Unit (TU) in the SAP system: 1) Press the 'Create' button, 2) Select a Carrier (optional), 3) Add Means of Transport (dummy = YVT1), 4) Add Packing Material (dummy = 6001006101), 5) Set Activity Direction to '2 Outbound', 6) Confirm by pressing 'Continue' or ENTER, and 7) Press the 'Save' button.

question: Can you summarize the key steps involved in the SAP S/4 Plan Transport – Export Process?
golden_answer: The key steps in the SAP S/4 Plan Transport – Export Process are: 1) Search for an existing Transportation Unit (TU) or create a new one, 2) Adjust TU header information, 3) Assign deliveries to the TU, 4) Optionally update ERP data and adjust TU item data, 5) Activate the TU, 6) Check outputs, 7) Trigger invoice creation, 8) Prepare customs declaration, and 9) Monitor and close the TU.

This comprehensive training provides an in-depth understanding of the Order to Cash (O2C) process, covering key elements such as sales order management, billing, delivery, and credit note processes. Participants will explore critical topics like number range definitions, organizational data, sales document types, item categories, partner functions, and message output. The course also delves into advanced functionalities like Vendor ATP (gATP), Dynamic Item Switch, and EWM execution. Additionally, quick reference cards for transaction codes and Fiori apps are included to streamline processes like sales, delivery, billing, and export management. This training is designed to equip participants with the knowledge and tools needed to efficiently manage O2C processes in SAP environments, ensuring seamless integration and execution of sales and billing operations.

Comprehensive Overview of General Elements in Order to Cash Process
This document provides a detailed summary of the 'General Elements' in the Order to Cash (O2C) process as implemented by Bosch Rexroth AG under the Grownfield project. It covers various aspects such as number range definitions, organizational data, sales document types, item categories, text schemes, partner functions, order reasons, rejection reasons, message output, and Vendor ATP (gATP).
1.1 Number Range Definition for Sales Order Documents
Defines number ranges for various sales document types, such as Standard Sales Orders (1*), Standard Scheduling Agreements (3*), and Credit/Debit Memo Requests (6*). Migration-specific number ranges like P1F* and P10* are also included.
1.2 Organizational Data (Sales Office, Sales Group)
Covers the characteristics and examples of organizational data such as Sales Office (destination of sales department) and Sales Group (sales department). Data can be manually maintained or preset via user profile parameters.
1.3 Sales Document Types
Lists various sales document types (e.g., YVB1 for Quotation Standard, YVC1 for Sales Order Standard, YVG1 for Customer Quantity Contract) with their descriptions and usage characteristics.
1.4 Item Categories
Explains how item categories are determined based on document type, item category group in the material master, and other factors. The corresponding item category can be automatically found and adjusted if necessary.
1.5 Text Scheme
Describes the usage of text fields in sales documents (Quotation, Sales Order, Delivery Note, Invoice) for printing, internal documentation, and communication. Includes details on text IDs, descriptions, and behaviors such as print relevance, copying to follow-up documents, and pop-up functionality.
1.6 Partner Functions
Outlines steps to manage sales-related information for business partners using SAP T-Code: BP. Includes roles like Sold-to-Party, Ship-to-Party, Payer, and Sales Employee, as well as external contact person relationships.
1.7 Order Reasons
Categorizes order reasons by document type (e.g., Free of Charge Orders, Internal Consumption Orders, Returns with Credit Note). Highlights their relevance for statistics, accounting, and tax determination. Examples include FC Commercial Goodwill (Y04) and BC Freight and Packaging Difference (Y53).
1.8 Rejection Reasons
Explains rejection reasons in sales documents, such as 'Canceled by Customer' (Y1) and 'Product No Longer Available' (Y4). Items with rejection reasons cannot be further processed. Rejection reasons are categorized by their billing and statistical relevance.
1.9 Message Output
Details the process of sending order confirmations automatically and electronically to customers or sales employees. Includes conditions for first confirmations and re-confirmations, as well as the use of condition records (e.g., Sales org./Sales DocTy/Sold-to).
1.10 Vendor ATP (gATP)
Covers the global ATP (gATP) process for checking vendor availability. Includes activation mechanisms based on Item Category Group (MTPOS) and Material Status (VMSTA). Examples include simulation of sales orders at vendor plants to determine delivery dates. Screenshots and diagrams illustrate the process.

This guide provides a detailed overview of handling scenarios where customers do not receive the full invoiced quantity of a product and the subsequent processes for free-of-charge deliveries and outbound delivery management in SAP. When a customer does not receive the full quantity, a free-of-charge order is created using sales order type YVI2 and item category YVF7. It is mandatory to enter internal reference information for this order type, and no ATP (Available-to-Promise) check is performed at the schedule line level, ensuring smoother processing. Before the picking process, stock must be built up using the NEGO transaction, after which the system automatically determines the source for picking the goods. Introduction: 2.5) Main Topics | Hints
DownPayment solution in S/4 is a Rexroth-wide solution in combination with the horizontal layer (PHL-system). The solution differs significantly from the solutions available in R/3. Since SAP plans to enhance only the 'billing plan' solution in the future, and not the 'condition-based solution', Bosch has decided to implement a solution incorporating the billing plan in S/4.
A customer places a sales order for high-value goods. Before delivery, the company requires a down payment to secure the order. In SAP, a DownPayment Request is created based on the billing plan in the sales order. Once the customer pays, the incoming payment clears the DownPayment Request and the DownPayment Invoice is created automatically. After delivery, the final billing document is generated, and revenue is posted. On the final invoice form, the received down payments are automatically listed and deducted from the customer’s final invoice amount.

Defines number ranges for various sales document types, such as Standard Sales Orders (1*), Standard Scheduling Agreements (3*), and Credit/Debit Memo Requests (6*). Migration-specific number ranges like P1F* and P10* are also included.

Covers the characteristics and examples of organizational data such as Sales Office (destination of sales department) and Sales Group (sales department). Data can be manually maintained or preset via user profile parameters.

Lists various sales document types (e.g., YVB1 for Quotation Standard, YVC1 for Sales Order Standard, YVG1 for Customer Quantity Contract) with their descriptions and usage characteristics.

Explains how item categories are determined based on document type, item category group in the material master, and other factors. The corresponding item category can be automatically found and adjusted if necessary.

Comprehensive Overview of General Elements in Order to Cash Process
This document provides a detailed summary of the 'General Elements' in the Order to Cash (O2C) process as implemented by Bosch Rexroth AG under the Grownfield project. It covers various aspects such as number range definitions, organizational data, sales document types, item categories, text schemes, partner functions, order reasons, rejection reasons, message output, and Vendor ATP (gATP).
1.1 Number Range Definition for Sales Order Documents
Defines number ranges for various sales document types, such as Standard Sales Orders (1*), Standard Scheduling Agreements (3*), and Credit/Debit Memo Requests (6*). Migration-specific number ranges like P1F* and P10* are also included.
1.2 Organizational Data (Sales Office, Sales Group)
Covers the characteristics and examples of organizational data such as Sales Office (destination of sales department) and Sales Group (sales department). Data can be manually maintained or preset via user profile parameters.
1.3 Sales Document Types
Lists various sales document types (e.g., YVB1 for Quotation Standard, YVC1 for Sales Order Standard, YVG1 for Customer Quantity Contract) with their descriptions and usage characteristics.
1.4 Item Categories
Explains how item categories are determined based on document type, item category group in the material master, and other factors. The corresponding item category can be automatically found and adjusted if necessary.
1.5 Text Scheme
Describes the usage of text fields in sales documents (Quotation, Sales Order, Delivery Note, Invoice) for printing, internal documentation, and communication. Includes details on text IDs, descriptions, and behaviors such as print relevance, copying to follow-up documents, and pop-up functionality.
1.6 Partner Functions
Outlines steps to manage sales-related information for business partners using SAP T-Code: BP. Includes roles like Sold-to-Party, Ship-to-Party, Payer, and Sales Employee, as well as external contact person relationships.
1.7 Order Reasons
Categorizes order reasons by document type (e.g., Free of Charge Orders, Internal Consumption Orders, Returns with Credit Note). Highlights their relevance for statistics, accounting, and tax determination. Examples include FC Commercial Goodwill (Y04) and BC Freight and Packaging Difference (Y53).
1.8 Rejection Reasons
Explains rejection reasons in sales documents, such as 'Canceled by Customer' (Y1) and 'Product No Longer Available' (Y4). Items with rejection reasons cannot be further processed. Rejection reasons are categorized by their billing and statistical relevance.
1.9 Message Output
Details the process of sending order confirmations automatically and electronically to customers or sales employees. Includes conditions for first confirmations and re-confirmations, as well as the use of condition records (e.g., Sales org./Sales DocTy/Sold-to).
1.10 Vendor ATP (gATP)
Covers the global ATP (gATP) process for checking vendor availability. Includes activation mechanisms based on Item Category Group (MTPOS) and Material Status (VMSTA). Examples include simulation of sales orders at vendor plants to determine delivery dates. Screenshots and diagrams illustrate the process.

DownPayment solution in S/4 is a Rexroth-wide solution in combination with the horizontal layer (PHL-system). The solution differs significantly from the solutions available in R/3. Since SAP plans to enhance only the 'billing plan' solution in the future, and not the 'condition-based solution', Bosch has decided to implement a solution incorporating the billing plan in S/4.
A customer places a sales order for high-value goods. Before delivery, the company requires a down payment to secure the order. In SAP, a DownPayment Request is created based on the billing plan in the sales order. Once the customer pays, the incoming payment clears the DownPayment Request and the DownPayment Invoice is created automatically. After delivery, the final billing document is generated, and revenue is posted. On the final invoice form, the received down payments are automatically listed and deducted from the customer’s final invoice amount.

This document provides a detailed summary of the 'General Elements' in the Order to Cash (O2C) process as implemented by Bosch Rexroth AG under the Grownfield project. It covers various aspects such as number range definitions, organizational data, sales document types, item categories, text schemes, partner functions, order reasons, rejection reasons, message output, and Vendor ATP (gATP).
1.1 Number Range Definition for Sales Order Documents
Defines number ranges for various sales document types, such as Standard Sales Orders (1*), Standard Scheduling Agreements (3*), and Credit/Debit Memo Requests (6*). Migration-specific number ranges like P1F* and P10* are also included.
1.2 Organizational Data (Sales Office, Sales Group)
Covers the characteristics and examples of organizational data such as Sales Office (destination of sales department) and Sales Group (sales department). Data can be manually maintained or preset via user profile parameters.
1.3 Sales Document Types
Lists various sales document types (e.g., YVB1 for Quotation Standard, YVC1 for Sales Order Standard, YVG1 for Customer Quantity Contract) with their descriptions and usage characteristics.
1.4 Item Categories
Explains how item categories are determined based on document type, item category group in the material master, and other factors. The corresponding item category can be automatically found and adjusted if necessary.
1.5 Text Scheme
Describes the usage of text fields in sales documents (Quotation, Sales Order, Delivery Note, Invoice) for printing, internal documentation, and communication. Includes details on text IDs, descriptions, and behaviors such as print relevance, copying to follow-up documents, and pop-up functionality.
1.6 Partner Functions
Outlines steps to manage sales-related information for business partners using SAP T-Code: BP. Includes roles like Sold-to-Party, Ship-to-Party, Payer, and Sales Employee, as well as external contact person relationships.
1.7 Order Reasons
Categorizes order reasons by document type (e.g., Free of Charge Orders, Internal Consumption Orders, Returns with Credit Note). Highlights their relevance for statistics, accounting, and tax determination. Examples include FC Commercial Goodwill (Y04) and BC Freight and Packaging Difference (Y53).
1.8 Rejection Reasons
Explains rejection reasons in sales documents, such as 'Canceled by Customer' (Y1) and 'Product No Longer Available' (Y4). Items with rejection reasons cannot be further processed. Rejection reasons are categorized by their billing and statistical relevance.
1.9 Message Output
Details the process of sending order confirmations automatically and electronically to customers or sales employees. Includes conditions for first confirmations and re-confirmations, as well as the use of condition records (e.g., Sales org./Sales DocTy/Sold-to).
1.10 Vendor ATP (gATP)
Covers the global ATP (gATP) process for checking vendor availability. Includes activation mechanisms based on Item Category Group (MTPOS) and Material Status (VMSTA). Process Overview - Full Correction
The concept of 'Full Correction' is implemented using a sequential pair of credit-/debit note types. The process involves the following steps:

1. A credit note with 100% of the value or quantity of the original billing document is posted with reference to the original invoice. This action completely reverses the original billing document.
2. A debit note with the new value or quantity is posted, creating a new billing document referencing the original invoice. 

The final result is either an increased or decreased version of the original billing document, which effectively serves as a specialized form of quantity correction. 

This approach is used to correct billing information beyond price and quantity, including text updates, tax IDs, and tax classification adjustments.

Additional logic ensures that a credit/debit note request cannot be created if the price is zero or negative, with an error message triggered in such cases.

Process Overview - Full Correction Example
A technical process represented by a sequence of credit and debit note types that must be posted to achieve full correction of an original billing document.
Credit Note Posting
Post a credit note with 100% value/quantity of the original billing document. Both sales order types reference the original invoice (YXK3). This action completely reverses the original billing document.
Debit Note Posting
Post a debit note with the new value/quantity. This creates the corrected billing document based on the original invoice reference (sales order type YXL1).
Produces a raised or reduced version of the original billing document, functioning as a quantity correction.
Applies to corrections of billing content beyond pricing and quantity, including texts, tax-IDs, and tax-classification.
Prevents credit/debit note request creation if the price is zero or negative. In such cases, an error message will be generated.

[O2C | O2C-04.030 Manage Debit Memo Request - Standard | Advanced]
Process Overview - Full Correction
The concept of 'Full Correction' is implemented using a sequential pair of credit-/debit note types. The process involves the following steps:

1. A credit note with 100% of the value or quantity of the original billing document is posted with reference to the original invoice. This action completely reverses the original billing document.
2. A debit note with the new value or quantity is posted, creating a new billing document referencing the original invoice. 

The final result is either an increased or decreased version of the original billing document, which effectively serves as a specialized form of quantity correction. 

This approach is used to correct billing information beyond price and quantity, including text updates, tax IDs, and tax classification adjustments.

Additional logic ensures that a credit/debit note request cannot be created if the price is zero or negative, with an error message triggered in such cases.

A billing correction is a scenario where an initial billing document from different end-to-end (E2E) processes must be corrected through a subsequent billing document.
In the 2-line correction (known as Faktura Correcta (2-item)), there is no need to distinguish between value/quantity or a full correction, as the 2-item variant works like a full correction by design.
First item is always a 100% reversal of the original item, and the second item specifies the new value/quantity.
Billing of Cost is only permissible for Billing of Costs invoice (YXM1) correction.
Additional logic prevents the creation of credit/debit note requests if the price is zero or negative. An error message will be triggered in these cases.

In contrast, value and quantity corrections involve issuing a credit note to adjust only the value or quantity of the original billing document without fully reversing it.

golden_answer: For a standard invoice correction, the Faktura Correcta (2-item) method can be used. A billing correction is defined as the process where an initial billing document from various E2E processes is corrected with a subsequent billing document. These corrections are relevant for all invoices requiring adjustments, excluding the correction documents themselves.
Additional mechanisms are implemented to prevent the creation of credit/debit note requests in cases where the price is zero or negative. An error message will be displayed for such scenarios.

[O2C | O2C-04.030 Manage Debit Memo Request - Standard | Advanced]
Process Overview - Full Correction
The concept of 'Full Correction' is implemented using a sequential pair of credit-/debit note types. The process involves the following steps:

1. A credit note with 100% of the value or quantity of the original billing document is posted with reference to the original invoice. This action completely reverses the original billing document.
2. A debit note with the new value or quantity is posted, creating a new billing document referencing the original invoice. 

The final result is either an increased or decreased version of the original billing document, which effectively serves as a specialized form of quantity correction. 

This approach is used to correct billing information beyond price and quantity, including text updates, tax IDs, and tax classification adjustments.

Additional logic ensures that a credit/debit note request cannot be created if the price is zero or negative, with an error message triggered in such cases.

question: What are the steps to create a Credit Memo Request for a DownPayment Invoice using transaction VA01?

golden_answer: The steps to create a Credit Memo Request using transaction VA01 are: 1) Create the memo request with transaction VA01 and select 'Create with Reference'; 2) Fill in the number of the relevant reference DownPayment invoice (YVM7); 3) Enter the customer reference and customer reference date; 4) Select the use-case-specific order reason (e.g., Y41 = BC Wrong Quantity/Price); 5) Adjust the refund on the item level by removing items not to be refunded or reducing the target quantity for partial refunds; 6) Save the request.

Process Overview - Full Correction
The concept of 'Full Correction' is implemented using a sequential pair of credit-/debit note types. The process involves the following steps:

1. A credit note with 100% of the value or quantity of the original billing document is posted with reference to the original invoice. This action completely reverses the original billing document.
2. A debit note with the new value or quantity is posted, creating a new billing document referencing the original invoice.

question: In what scenarios would you apply the 2-line debit memo process, and how would you handle cases where the price is zero or negative?
golden_answer: The 2-line debit memo process is applied for standard invoice corrections (e.g., YVM1, YVM8) but cannot be used for down payment invoice corrections (YVM7) or ARM credit notes (YVH2). If the price is zero or negative, the system prevents the creation of the debit memo request and displays an error message.

Process Overview - 1.4) Good to know | Definition
This slide provides information about billing correction scenarios in E2E processes. A billing correction involves correcting an initial billing document with a subsequent billing document. The '2line correction' method (Faktura Correcta - 2-item) simplifies the process by functioning as a full correction by design: the first item reverses the original item completely (100%), while the second item defines the new value or quantity. It highlights that 'Debit Memo Request Billing of Cost' is exclusively allowed for the correction of 'Billing of Costs invoice (YXM1).' Furthermore, it emphasizes that additional logic prevents credit/debit note request creation when the price is zero or negative, triggering an error message in such cases.

This document provides a detailed overview of the 'Billing of Costs - Debit Memo Request (2-Line)' process within the Order to Cash (O2C) workflow, as implemented by Rexroth, a Bosch Company. The process is part of the GROWNFIELD program, which emphasizes the integration of People, Technology, and Processes.
Process Overview
Introduction to the billing of costs and debit memo request processes.
Key business roles involved include Shipping Clerk, Packer, Loader, Shipping Specialist, SD SOM, MRP-Controller, and S & O Planner.
The process involves managing debit memo requests (L4) with steps such as initialization, justification checks, and creating/changing credit memo requests.
Future Process: Debit Memo Request (2-Line)
A streamlined 2-line correction process for billing adjustments.
Key steps include creating a credit memo, entering reference invoice details, customer references, selecting use case-specific reasons, entering corrections in line 2, and saving the request.
The process is supported by SAP transaction VA01 and includes specific order types, item categories, and distribution channels.
Key Definitions and Logic
Billing corrections involve creating a subsequent billing document to correct an initial one.
The 2-line correction method simplifies the process by reversing the original item and defining the new value or quantity in a second line.
Additional logic prevents credit/debit note creation for zero or negative prices, triggering error messages in such cases.

Comprehensive Overview of General Elements in Order to Cash Process
This document provides a detailed summary of the 'General Elements' in the Order to Cash (O2C) process as implemented by Bosch Rexroth AG under the Grownfield project. It covers various aspects such as number range definitions, organizational data, sales document types, item categories, text schemes, partner functions, order reasons, rejection reasons, message output, and Vendor ATP (gATP).
1.1 Number Range Definition for Sales Order Documents
Defines number ranges for various sales document types, such as Standard Sales Orders (1*), Standard Scheduling Agreements (3*), and Credit/Debit Memo Requests (6*). Migration-specific number ranges like P1F* and P10* are also included.
1.2 Organizational Data (Sales Office, Sales Group)
Covers the characteristics and examples of organizational data such as Sales Office (destination of sales department) and Sales Group (sales department). Data can be manually maintained or preset via user profile parameters.
1.3 Sales Document Types
Lists various sales document types (e.g., YVB1 for Quotation Standard, YVC1 for Sales Order Standard, YVG1 for Customer Quantity Contract) with their descriptions and usage characteristics.
1.4 Item Categories
Explains how item categories are determined based on document type, item category group in the material master, and other factors. The corresponding item category can be automatically found and adjusted if necessary.
1.5 Text Scheme
Describes the usage of text fields in sales documents (Quotation, Sales Order, Delivery Note, Invoice) for printing, internal documentation, and communication. Includes details on text IDs, descriptions, and behaviors such as print relevance, copying to follow-up documents, and pop-up functionality.
1.6 Partner Functions
Outlines steps to manage sales-related information for business partners using SAP T-Code: BP. Includes roles like Sold-to-Party, Ship-to-Party, Payer, and Sales Employee, as well as external contact person relationships.
1.7 Order Reasons
Categorizes order reasons by document type (e.g., Free of Charge Orders, Internal Consumption Orders, Returns with Credit Note). Highlights their relevance for statistics, accounting, and tax determination. Examples include FC Commercial Goodwill (Y04) and BC Freight and Packaging Difference (Y53).
1.8 Rejection Reasons
Explains rejection reasons in sales documents, such as 'Canceled by Customer' (Y1) and 'Product No Longer Available' (Y4). Items with rejection reasons cannot be further processed. Rejection reasons are categorized by their billing and statistical relevance.
1.9 Message Output
Details the process of sending order confirmations automatically and electronically to customers or sales employees. Includes conditions for first confirmations and re-confirmations, as well as the use of condition records (e.g., Sales org./Sales DocTy/Sold-to).
1.10 Vendor ATP (gATP)
Covers the global ATP (gATP) process for checking vendor availability. Includes activation mechanisms based on Item Category Group (MTPOS) and Material Status (VMSTA). Examples include simulation of sales orders at vendor plants to determine delivery dates. Screenshots and diagrams illustrate the process.
The content is branded under Bosch Rexroth AG and its Grownfield project, with logos and copyright information included throughout the slides.

Process Overview - 1.4) Good to know | Definition
A billing correction refers to correcting an initial billing document from various End-to-End (E2E) processes with a subsequent billing document.
The 2-line correction, also known as Faktura Correcta (2-item), functions as a full correction without distinguishing between Value/Quantity.
In the 2-item variant, the first item always provides a 100% reversal of the original item, while the second item establishes the new value/quantity.
Faktura Correcta can only be applied to standard invoice corrections (YVM1, YVM8) but not for Down Payment invoice corrections (YVM7) or ARM credit notes (YVH2), among others.
Additional logic is implemented to block credit/debit note request creation in cases where the price is zero or negative, resulting in an error message.

A billing correction is a scenario, which describes the case when an initial billing document from

generated_answer:
The Vendor ATP (gATP) process during sales order execution involves an automatic availability check for sales order items. When a sales order is created, the system simulates the order at the vendor plant to determine the delivery date and material availability, rather than relying on the standard planned delivery time from purchasing info records. This check is activated based on the item category group and material status.

Key steps include:
1. **Automatic Execution**: The availability check is triggered automatically during the sales order item execution.
2. **Simulation**: The system simulates the sales order at the vendor's location to ascertain the confirmed delivery date and availability date.
3. **Fallback Mechanism**: If the gATP check fails, the system can revert to local ATP checks to ensure material availability.
4. **Display of Results**: The confirmed delivery date and material availability date are displayed in the sales order details, providing essential information for order fulfillment.

This process ensures that the delivery dates provided to customers are accurate and based on real-time vendor capabilities.
