Comprehensive Summary of Customer Return Order Management
This document provides a detailed guide on managing customer return orders within the Order-to-Cash (O2C) process, focusing on standard situations, special cases, and specific scenarios like Indradrive returns. It includes process flows, transaction codes, return reasons, and logistical follow-ups, supported by visual aids and branding elements from Bosch Rexroth AG.
General Description
Covers the scope, rules, involved parties, and process documentation for customer returns. It highlights use cases such as wrong orders, late deliveries, and recalls, while excluding service/repair and logistic claims. The Advanced Returns Management (ARM) system is introduced as the foundation for the process.
Process Flow
Outlines the high-level steps in the customer returns process: creating return orders, returns delivery, material inspection, logistical follow-up, customer refund, and billing. Visual diagrams illustrate the interconnected steps under the 'Returns Overview' umbrella.
Main Transaction Codes
Lists key SAP transaction codes such as VA01 (Create Return Order), VF01 (Create Billing Document), MSR_CRD (Customer Refund Determination), and /SCWM/PRDI (Book Goods Receipt), among others, to facilitate process execution.
Important Process Parameters
Details critical parameters like order type (YVH2), refund type (Credit Memo), item categories (YVR2, YVR4), and approval frameworks. It also lists return and order reasons with corresponding codes for accurate documentation.
Step-by-Step Guidelines
Create Quality Notification (optional) using QM01.
Create Return Order with VA01, using references for data accuracy.
Maintain return reasons and order reasons.
Check and update pricing with condition type ZPEK.
Save the return order, which will be subject to approval.
Monitor the return order status using MSR_TRC_C.
Create a Credit Memo Request (MSR_CRD) and Credit Note (VF01).
Screenshots and diagrams illustrate the SAP interface and process steps.
If return delivery is not created, cancel return order items.
If return delivery is created, cancel inbound delivery in EWM and reject items in the return order.
Use MSR_CRD to set rejection reasons for items.
Rejected items are updated in the Credit Memo Request screen.
Create return order without reference.
Attach price screenshots and adapt values manually.
Complete approval via the framework.
Handle delivery-relevant items manually.
Cancel price-relevant header items and higher-level assignments.
ARM cannot handle HPOS/UPOS cases effectively, and current solutions are suboptimal.
Transfer to Free Available Stock
Handle main items only; sub-items remain in Indradrive storage.
Transfer to Scrap
Scrapping of Indradrive items must be done manually.
Send Back to Customer
Process not possible via ARM; items must be double-checked before goods receipt and returned immediately if not acceptable.
Ship to Vendor
Use 'Transfer to Free Available Stock' and create a separate return purchase order.
Resale of Indradrive items is currently not possible until the SFS process is implemented. The process will be revisited in the future.
Logistical Follow-Up
Describes process variants such as shipping to vendors, sending items back to customers, scrapping, and moving items to unrestricted stock. Status indicators (green, yellow, red, gray) are used to track process completion.
Visual and Branding Elements
The slides feature the Bosch Rexroth AG logo, Grownfield emblem, and abstract designs symbolizing connectivity and process flow. Screenshots of SAP interfaces and process diagrams are included for clarity.

This slide outlines information regarding the VL10 transaction, which can be executed in two scenarios: Dialogue Mode and Background Mode. 

1. **Background Mode**: 
   - Commonly used for regular jobs (e.g., overnight). 
   - Automatically tries to combine as many order items as possible into deliveries. 
   - No user adjustments can be made; all deliveries are created automatically based on predefined rules. 

2. **Dialogue Mode**: 
   - Equivalent to the manual execution using VL01n.
   - Allows users to select multiple orders for delivery together. 
   - VL10 creates deliveries sequentially, enabling users to make adjustments to each delivery before saving. 
   - After saving one delivery, another delivery is created automatically, allowing further adjustments.

DC Standard Process for Creating Outbound Deliveries
This video demonstrates the DC standard process for creating outbound deliveries, focusing on both manual and automated methods. Outbound deliveries can be created manually using transaction VL01N or automatically via transaction VL10, which is the proposed standard process. The automated process in VL10 has stricter delivery creation rules compared to manual creation, ensuring consistency in criteria such as INCA terms, shipping conditions, and ship-to details. Users can adjust selection criteria, such as shipping point and user roles, in VL10 before executing the delivery creation. The process allows for selecting specific sales order items for delivery, and logs can be reviewed to verify successful creation or identify issues. In cases where automated delivery creation is not possible due to errors or delivery group constraints, manual creation via VL01N is required. After creation, users can verify mandatory header fields, check delivery notes or packing texts, and confirm the status of the outbound delivery order in the EWM system. A successful delivery creation indicates that the delivery is released, with no GTS block, and warehouse tasks can proceed to picking. The video highlights the flexibility and specific settings available in both automated and manual delivery creation processes.

This document provides a detailed guide to the 'Order to Cash' (O2C) process, focusing on the 'Prepare Outbound Delivery' procedure within Bosch Rexroth AG's logistics operations as part of the 'Grownfield' initiative. [O2C | O2C-03.012 Prepare Outbound delivery - additional video | Advanced]
DC Standard Process for Creating Outbound Deliveries
This video demonstrates the DC standard process for creating outbound deliveries, focusing on both manual and automated methods. Outbound deliveries can be created manually using transaction VL01N or automatically via transaction VL10, which is the proposed standard process. The automated process in VL10 has stricter delivery creation rules compared to manual creation, ensuring consistency in criteria such as INCA terms, shipping conditions, and ship-to details. Users can adjust selection criteria, such as shipping point and user roles, in VL10 before executing the delivery creation. The process allows for selecting specific sales order items for delivery, and logs can be reviewed to verify successful creation or identify issues. In cases where automated delivery creation is not possible due to errors or delivery group constraints, manual creation via VL01N is required. After creation, users can verify mandatory header fields, check delivery notes or packing texts, and confirm the status of the outbound delivery order in the EWM system. A successful delivery creation indicates that the delivery is released, with no GTS block, and warehouse tasks can proceed to picking. The video highlights the flexibility and specific settings available in both automated and manual delivery creation processes.

Transaction
Description
/SCWM/TU
In SAP EWM, the transaction /SCWM/TU is used to manage the shipping process by 
creating a freight document. This document groups together multiple outbound deliveries 
that are shipped using the same means of transport, such as a truck or container. Deliveries 
are assigned to the freight document based on common criteria like destination or route. 
Once the goods are loaded, the system records the loading and departure, and finally, the 
goods issue is posted. This process ensures efficient handling, tracking, and 
documentation of outbound shipments.
VL02n
The transaction VL02N (Change Outbound Delivery) in SAP ERP is used to update 
outbound deliveries. In the context of transport loading, it allows users e.g. to manually 
confirm the loading of goods, update delivery quantities, assign handling units, and post the 
goods issue. This step is essential to finalize the delivery process and trigger the transfer of 
ownership and inventory reduction.

DC Standard Process for Creating Outbound Deliveries
This video demonstrates the DC standard process for creating outbound deliveries, focusing on both manual and automated methods. Outbound deliveries can be created manually using transaction VL01N or automatically via transaction VL10, which is the proposed standard process. The automated process in VL10 has stricter delivery creation rules compared to manual creation, ensuring consistency in criteria such as INCA terms, shipping conditions, and ship-to details. Users can adjust selection criteria, such as shipping point and user roles, in VL10 before executing the delivery creation. The process allows for selecting specific sales order items for delivery, and logs can be reviewed to verify successful creation or identify issues. In cases where automated delivery creation is not possible due to errors or delivery group constraints, manual creation via VL01N is required. After creation, users can verify mandatory header fields, check delivery notes or packing texts, and confirm the status of the outbound delivery order in the EWM system. A successful delivery creation indicates that the delivery is released, with no GTS block, and warehouse tasks can proceed to picking. The video highlights the flexibility and specific settings available in both automated and manual delivery creation processes.

This document provides an in-depth guide to SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) monitoring and reporting processes, as implemented by Bosch Rexroth AG. 6. **Storage Bin Monitoring**: Managing blocked storage bins and monitoring intermediate storage types like GR and GI zones.

Credit Note Posting
Post a credit note with 100% value/quantity of the original billing document. Both sales order types reference the original invoice (YXK3). This action completely reverses the original billing document.
Debit Note Posting
Post a debit note with the new value/quantity. This creates the corrected billing document based on the original invoice reference (sales order type YXL1).

[O2C | O2C-04.031 Manage Debit Memo Request - 2line | Advanced]
Process Overview - 1.4) Good to know | Definition
A billing correction refers to correcting an initial billing document from various End-to-End (E2E) processes with a subsequent billing document.
The 2-line correction, also known as Faktura Correcta (2-item), functions as a full correction without distinguishing between Value/Quantity.
In the 2-item variant, the first item always provides a 100% reversal of the original item, while the second item establishes the new value/quantity.
Faktura Correcta can only be applied to standard invoice corrections (YVM1, YVM8) but not for Down Payment invoice corrections (YVM7) or ARM credit notes (YVH2), among others.
Additional logic is implemented to block credit/debit note request creation in cases where the price is zero or negative, resulting in an error message.

Process Overview - 1.4) Good to know | Definition
A billing correction is a scenario where an initial billing document from different end-to-end (E2E) processes must be corrected through a subsequent billing document.
In the 2-line correction (known as Faktura Correcta (2-item)), there is no need to distinguish between value/quantity or a full correction, as the 2-item variant works like a full correction by design.
First item is always a 100% reversal of the original item, and the second item specifies the new value/quantity.
Billing of Cost is only permissible for Billing of Costs invoice (YXM1) correction.
Additional logic prevents the creation of credit/debit note requests if the price is zero or negative. An error message will be triggered in these cases.

Process Overview | 1.1 Good to know | Definition
SAP S/4HANA provides a comprehensive Service Contract Management capability enabling long-term service agreements with customers. These contracts cover fixed recurring fees, entitlements, billing automation, renewals, and integration with service execution. Service contract management handles two business cases: 1) Billing of recurring fixed fees under the contract, and 2) Service orders for extra activities, spare parts, travel, or consumption that are outside the contracted scope.
Fixed Recurring Services
Customers can avail regular recurring services against a fixed period rate contract. Billing is handled via contract documents as per the predefined billing plan. Costs are settled to the contract item.
Additional Services
Customers can be billed for additional services not included in the fixed fee contract. Billing is done using service orders instead of the contract billing plan. However, the costs and revenues are settled to the contract item.

Comprehensive Overview of General Elements in Order to Cash Process
This document provides a detailed summary of the 'General Elements' in the Order to Cash (O2C) process as implemented by Bosch Rexroth AG under the Grownfield project. It covers various aspects such as number range definitions, organizational data, sales document types, item categories, text schemes, partner functions, order reasons, rejection reasons, message output, and Vendor ATP (gATP).
1.1 Number Range Definition for Sales Order Documents
Defines number ranges for various sales document types, such as Standard Sales Orders (1*), Standard Scheduling Agreements (3*), and Credit/Debit Memo Requests (6*). Migration-specific number ranges like P1F* and P10* are also included.
1.2 Organizational Data (Sales Office, Sales Group)
Covers the characteristics and examples of organizational data such as Sales Office (destination of sales department) and Sales Group (sales department). Data can be manually maintained or preset via user profile parameters.
1.3 Sales Document Types
Lists various sales document types (e.g., YVB1 for Quotation Standard, YVC1 for Sales Order Standard, YVG1 for Customer Quantity Contract) with their descriptions and usage characteristics.
1.4 Item Categories
Explains how item categories are determined based on document type, item category group in the material master, and other factors. The corresponding item category can be automatically found and adjusted if necessary.
1.5 Text Scheme
Describes the usage of text fields in sales documents (Quotation, Sales Order, Delivery Note, Invoice) for printing, internal documentation, and communication. Includes details on text IDs, descriptions, and behaviors such as print relevance, copying to follow-up documents, and pop-up functionality.
1.6 Partner Functions
Outlines steps to manage sales-related information for business partners using SAP T-Code: BP. Includes roles like Sold-to-Party, Ship-to-Party, Payer, and Sales Employee, as well as external contact person relationships.
1.7 Order Reasons
Categorizes order reasons by document type (e.g., Free of Charge Orders, Internal Consumption Orders, Returns with Credit Note). Highlights their relevance for statistics, accounting, and tax determination. Examples include FC Commercial Goodwill (Y04) and BC Freight and Packaging Difference (Y53).
1.8 Rejection Reasons
Explains rejection reasons in sales documents, such as 'Canceled by Customer' (Y1) and 'Product No Longer Available' (Y4). Items with rejection reasons cannot be further processed. Rejection reasons are categorized by their billing and statistical relevance.
1.9 Message Output
Details the process of sending order confirmations automatically and electronically to customers or sales employees. Includes conditions for first confirmations and re-confirmations, as well as the use of condition records (e.g., Sales org./Sales DocTy/Sold-to).
1.10 Vendor ATP (gATP)
Covers the global ATP (gATP) process for checking vendor availability. Includes activation mechanisms based on Item Category Group (MTPOS) and Material Status (VMSTA). Examples include simulation of sales orders at vendor plants to determine delivery dates. Screenshots and diagrams illustrate the process.
The content is branded under Bosch Rexroth AG and its Grownfield project, with logos and copyright information included throughout the slides.

Process Overview | 1.1 Good to know | Definition
SAP S/4HANA provides a comprehensive Service Contract Management capability enabling long-term service agreements with customers. These contracts cover fixed recurring fees, entitlements, billing automation, renewals, and integration with service execution. Service contract management handles two business cases: 1) Billing of recurring fixed fees under the contract, and 2) Service orders for extra activities, spare parts, travel, or consumption that are outside the contracted scope.
Fixed Recurring Services
Customers can avail regular recurring services against a fixed period rate contract. Billing is handled via contract documents as per the predefined billing plan. Costs are settled to the contract item.
Additional Services
Customers can be billed for additional services not included in the fixed fee contract. Billing is done using service orders instead of the contract billing plan. However, the costs and revenues are settled to the contract item.

question: What is the purpose of the EMORD transaction code in EDI IDoc Monitoring?
golden_answer: The EMORD transaction code is used to monitor IDocs (Intermediate Documents) related to Sales and Distribution (SD) orders. It allows users to check the status of IDocs sent from the SAP system to external systems, such as customers or vendors, and provides functionalities to view details about each IDoc, including sender, receiver, and message type, as well as to resend failed or rejected IDocs.

Overview:

EMORD is an SAP transaction code used to monitor IDocs (Intermediate Documents) for Sales and 
Distribution (SD) orders.

It is used to check the status of IDocs that have been sent from the SAP system to external systems, 
such as customers or vendors.

Functionality:

The EMORD transaction code allows users to view the status of IDocs that have been sent from the 
SAP system.
▪
It also allows users to view the details of each IDoc, such as the sender, receiver, and message type. 
Additionally, users can use this transaction code to resend IDocs that have failed or been rejected.

question: What does the term SDD stand for and what are its main purposes?
golden_answer: SDD stands for Semi-Direct Delivery. Its main purposes are to enable fast, sustainable, and cost-efficient delivery from the delivery plant to customers, and to reduce inventories and warehousing costs in Country Units (CUs) by ensuring sales to customers via the responsible CU, as required by DC sales strategy or legal requirements.

question: How do you release stock from a handling unit (HU) using the /SCWM/CANCPICK transaction?
golden_source: O2C-03.063 Reverse Processing - Assignment to HU.pptx
golden_answer: To release stock from a handling unit (HU) using /SCWM/CANCPICK: (1) Open the transaction /SCWM/CANCPICK, (2) search for the affected delivery or HU, (3) navigate to the 'Handling Units' tab, (4) double-click on the related handling unit(s), (5) check if the content is correct, (6) click the button 'Release Stock + HU WT Foreground,' and (7) a new window will open showing the created warehouse tasks.

question: How do you reverse a goods issue in a Transportation Unit (TU) using SAP S/4?
golden_source: O2C-03.064 Reverse Processing - Goods Issue Done.pptx
golden_answer: To reverse a goods issue in a Transportation Unit (TU), open transaction /SCWM/TU, search for the related Outbound Delivery, select the header line, click on the dropdown button at 'Goods Issue,' select 'Reverse Goods Issue,' and press 'Save.' This reverses the goods issue for all related deliveries.

question: How can handling units be repacked if goods are damaged during the reverse processing workflow?
golden_source: O2C-03.064 Reverse Processing - Goods Issue Done.pptx
golden_answer: Damaged goods can be repacked by opening transaction /SCWM/MON, searching for the related Outbound Delivery, selecting the respective line, clicking the 'Handling Unit' button, and checking item information. Then, create a warehouse task, enter warehouse process type 3080, confirm, and repack the goods at the packing station.

Guide to Packing Goods for Outbound Shipping in SAP EWM
This guide provides an overview of the process for packing goods for outbound shipping using SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM). The process begins by accessing the transaction `scwm.pack` and selecting the warehouse number and outbound delivery order in the warehouse request field. The packer typically receives a picking list and manually checks for any order-related packing information, as there are no automatic flags or pop-ups for such details. Delivery items are packed into shipping handling units (HUs) by selecting the material, choosing appropriate packaging material, and using drag-and-drop functionality. If an item does not fit into the current handling unit, it must be split, and a new handling unit is created. The system can automatically pre-fill the new handling unit, and the packer can adjust the weight, volume, and dimensions as needed. Once packed, the handling unit label is printed, and the process is finalized in the packing monitor. This triggers background activities such as determining the forwarder, updating the ERP outbound delivery, and preparing the goods for physical movement to the staging area. The process may vary depending on the warehouse structure and organization.

1. **Cancel Material Document**: Reverse document processing stages and generate reversal documents (movement type 601).
2. **Delete Actual Date for SiT**: Navigate to SAP transactions (e.g., VL02n) to delete shipment and delivery dates.
3. **Reverse Goods Issue**: Use SAP transactions (/SCWM/FD and /SCWM/TU) to reverse goods issues for specific or all related deliveries.
4. **Reverse Loading**: Update the status of transportation units (TU) to 'Unloaded', noting limitations on unloading all deliveries at once.
5. **Change TU Status to 'Planned'**: Reverse arrival and save the TU status.
6. **Adjust Transport Planning**: Unassign deliveries from TUs if necessary.
7. **Process Handling Units**: Repack or cancel handling units based on business needs, including deleting EWM outbound deliveries and releasing stock from handling units.

These steps must be executed in the same sequence they were completed, with special authorizations and configurations required for certain actions.

The transition from SAP R/3 to S/4 HANA improves MRP parameter standardization and process efficiency through several key enhancements:

1. **Standardization of MRP Parameters**: S/4 HANA emphasizes the standardization of MRP parameters, which simplifies the configuration and management of material master data. This includes the creation of suggestion lists and catalogs for optimized variants, ensuring consistency across the system.

2. **Statistical Data Analysis**: A comprehensive statistical analysis of current R/3 systems provides insights into existing configurations, allowing for informed decisions on parameter settings in S/4 HANA.

3. **Centralized Catalogs**: The introduction of centralized catalogs for MRP types, lot sizes, planning calendars, and special procurement types facilitates easier access and selection of parameters tailored to specific business needs.

4. **Customization Options**: While SAP standard variants are preferred, S/4 HANA allows for customized variants when standard options do not meet business requirements, enhancing flexibility and adaptability.

5. **Improved User Experience**: The use of the Fiori app 'Master Data Display (MDD)' in S/4 HANA provides a more intuitive interface for displaying and managing material master data, improving user efficiency.

6. **Future Configurations**: The focus on future configurations for MRP settings and forecasting enhances the ability to adapt to changing business needs and improves overall planning accuracy.

These improvements collectively lead to more efficient procurement and planning workflows, reducing errors and increasing operational efficiency.

[P2P | P2P-02.010 Material Planning | Advanced]
Changes in Process - 3.2. Quota Arrangement
In the S/4 HANA environment, the 'quota arrangement usage' field does not need to be activated. It is automatically considered by the MRP during the material requirement planning process. When a quota arrangement is maintained via the MEQ1 transaction for a material, Standard SAP will consistently apply it for source determination during MRP runs. Visual representations display the transition from R3 to S4 systems, highlighting differences where the quota arrangement usage field is no longer valid. Key focus areas include procurement processes in the material requirement planning system.

The transition from SAP R3 to S/4 HANA impacts the material planning process by introducing several key changes:

1. **Reorder Point Planning**: Updates to MRP types allow for both manual and automatic reorder point calculations, enhancing efficiency in inventory management.

2. **Quota Arrangement**: In S/4 HANA, the quota arrangement usage field is automatically considered during MRP runs, eliminating the need for manual activation.

3. **Subcontracting Process**: Enhancements include the use of MRP areas and special procurement types, streamlining subcontracting operations.

4. **Automation and Optimization**: The future state of material planning in S/4 HANA emphasizes automated processes for material requirements, BOM resolution, and net demand planning, leading to improved decision-making for 'make' or 'buy' processes.

5. **Monitoring and Management**: The system provides automated and manual steps for monitoring material planning, including availability checks and exception handling, which enhances overall operational efficiency.

These changes reflect a modernization of the material planning process, focusing on integration, automation, and improved user experience through tools like Fiori apps.

question: What are the steps involved in monitoring the material planning situation in SAP S/4 HANA?
golden_answer: The steps include checking the criticality of materials based on availability, net demand calculation, stock coverage time, exception indicators, and stock value within a defined time period. Material planners clarify the delivery situation for critical materials and update MRP elements if there are deviations in the planning situation.

Material Planning Processes - Monitoring Planning Situation
4.4 Monitoring Planning Situation
Key steps in the monitoring of the material planning situation, some of which are automated by SAP.
After MRP elements are created or updated, the criticality of the material is checked based on the following:
Availability check (Missing Parts Fiori App in T1R System)
Net demand calculation (Tbd)
Stock coverage time (Tbd)
Exception indicator (Tbd)
Value of stock within defined time period (Tbd)
The delivery situation is clarified according to critical materials by the material planner.
If there is a deviation in the planning situation, the MRP element should be updated by the material planner.
Processes related to material planning and monitoring are part of the 'Procure to Pay' workflow.

Inspection Execution
Quality inspectors record results against the characteristics defined in the inspection plan.

question: How can alternative packaging instructions be used for different delivery quantities?
golden_answer: Alternative packaging instructions can be used to specify different packaging requirements based on delivery quantities. For example, one packaging instruction can be created for quantities between 1 to 59 pieces, and another for 60 to 100 pieces. The order of the instructions is important, with the instruction for higher quantities listed first.

question: What are the key differences between SAP R/3 and SAP S/4HANA in terms of stock management and usage decisions?
golden_answer: In SAP R/3, stock management is focused on Inventory Management (IM) at the storage location level, while SAP S/4HANA introduces Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) for detailed warehouse operations, including goods movement and resource optimization. SAP R/3 supports usage decisions (UD) only at the lot level, whereas SAP S/4HANA enables UD at both the lot and handling unit (HU) levels. Additionally, SAP S/4HANA offers automatic usage decisions for skip lots and results marked as OK, as well as destructive inspections at the HU level.

This slide explains the concept of Dynamic Modification Rule (DMR) in SAP Quality Management (QM) and its implementation at Bosch Rexroth. DMR is a configuration setting in SAP QM that enables dynamic adjustment of the inspection scope based on the results of previous inspections. This results in the system automatically switching between different inspection stages, such as 'tightened,' 'normal,' 'reduced,' or 'skip,' depending on whether previous inspection lots were accepted or rejected.

A DMR can be configured to reduce inspection efforts and costs when consecutive inspections pass successfully by switching to 'reduced' or 'skip' stages. Conversely, if inspections fail, the system adjusts to a 'tightened' inspection stage to ensure quality.

Key application areas of DMR include:
- Lot level (header or characteristic level).
- Inspection type level in the material master QM view inspection setup.

At Bosch Rexroth, the DMR is implemented only at the characteristic level.

The slide also features a diagram illustrating the progression of inspection stages (tightened, normal, reduced, skip) over time, based on pass or fail results in inspection lots.

question: How can handling units (HUs) be split into accepted, rejected, or scrapped portions during the usage decision process?
golden_answer: Handling units (HUs) can be split during the usage decision process by creating new HUs for the rejected or scrapped portions. Each HU is then assigned a specific usage decision, such as accepted, rejected, or scrapped, and follow-up activities are triggered accordingly.

question: What are the key differences between SAP R/3 and SAP S/4HANA in terms of creating manual inspection lots and using the Q-Module?

The function supports various scenarios for processing quality certificates during and after goods receipt.
Certificate is received at goods receipt
When the receipt is confirmed: the certificate status is set to 'Received'.
If no further certificate check is needed and an inspection lot is created, its status becomes 'CROK' (certificate receipt confirmed).
When the receipt is not confirmed: the certificate status is set to 'Expected'.
If an inspection lot is created under these circumstances, its status will be 'CTCM' (certificate confirmation missing).
Certificate for purchase order item received after goods receipt
Two options for confirmation:
1) Confirmation with the usage decision or partial usage decision.
2) Confirmation using the transaction to change a certificate receipt.
For confirmation, either the purchase order number and item or the material document number and corresponding document are required.
Processing reminders for missing certificates

The function supports various scenarios for processing quality certificates during and after goods receipt.
Certificate is received at goods receipt
When the receipt is confirmed: the certificate status is set to 'Received'.
If no further certificate check is needed and an inspection lot is created, its status becomes 'CROK' (certificate receipt confirmed).
When the receipt is not confirmed: the certificate status is set to 'Expected'.
If an inspection lot is created under these circumstances, its status will be 'CTCM' (certificate confirmation missing).
Certificate for purchase order item received after goods receipt
Two options for confirmation:
1) Confirmation with the usage decision or partial usage decision.
2) Confirmation using the transaction to change a certificate receipt.
For confirmation, either the purchase order number and item or the material document number and corresponding document are required.
Processing reminders for missing certificates
Generate reminders for certificates not yet received based on the certificate receipt status.
Reminders can be triggered after the goods receipt date plus the reminder period has passed.
Users can select the objects for which they want to generate reminders, which are created using a SAP script form.

question: Can you summarize the process for handling quality certificates during goods receipt, including scenarios for missing certificates?
golden_answer: During goods receipt, the system creates an inspection lot and assigns a status based on the certificate submission. If the certificate is received, the status is set to CROK (Certificate Receipt Confirmed), allowing the usage decision. If the certificate is missing, the status is set to CTCM (Certificate Confirmation Missing), blocking the usage decision until the certificate is recorded. Reminders for missing certificates can be generated using transaction QC55.

question: What are the two main categories of supplier returns and their specific handling procedures?
golden_answer: The two main categories of supplier returns are: 1) 'Return of Good Material,' which applies to materials that are physically sound but returned due to reasons such as over-shipment, order cancellation, or end-of-life inventory management, and 2) 'Return Due to Complaint/Defect,' which involves materials that do not meet quality standards, are defective, damaged, incorrect, or otherwise non-conforming, requiring a formal complaint to the supplier.

question: What are the steps to create a return purchase order (PO) manually for a supplier return from stock?
golden_answer: To create a return PO manually for a supplier return from stock: 1) Use transaction ME21N and enter header information such as Order Type NB2, Supplier, Purchasing Organization, Purchasing Group, and Company Code. 2) Add relevant item data like Material, PO Quantity, and SAP Plant Code. 3) Ensure the 'returns item' checkbox is set. 4) Check delivery-relevant information, including stock type (set to 'S' for Blocked Stock) and shipping details. 5) Verify and fill in Incoterms and save the purchase order.

question: What are the key roles and responsibilities of different business functions in managing supplier returns?
golden_answer: Key roles and responsibilities include: 1) Purchasing/Procurement: Initiates and manages communication with suppliers regarding returns. 2) Warehouse/Logistics: Handles physical inspection, segregation, packaging, and shipment of returned goods. 3) Quality Assurance (QA): Identifies non-conforming materials and provides technical justification for quality-related returns. 4) Finance/Accounts Payable: Processes credit notes and ensures accurate financial reconciliation. 5) Production/Operations: Identifies material issues necessitating returns and provides operational context.

This presentation by Bosch Rexroth, titled 'Information to Order (I2O),' provides a comprehensive overview of master data and its interdependencies within the I2O process. The slides cover various aspects of master data, including Customer Master Data, Material Master Data, Price Master, Output Master, and Material Determination, emphasizing their roles in ensuring efficient and error-free business transactions. Key topics include:

1. **Customer Master Data and Partner Functions**: Details customer information (e.g., name, address, payment terms) and partner roles (e.g., Sold-to Party, Ship-to Party) used in sales, shipping, and billing processes. Key transactions (BP, KN* tables) and partner function applications in sales orders and deliveries are highlighted.

2. **Material Master Data**: Serves as the central source for material-related data, including material type, division, and pricing group. Relevant views (Basic Data, Sales Org Data) and transactions (MM01, MM02) are outlined.

3. **Price Master**: Manages pricing, discounts, and surcharges through condition records, access sequences, and pricing procedures. Key condition types (e.g., ZGLP, ZDBA) and their SAP tables (e.g., A118, A602) are detailed.

4. **Output Master**: Controls how documents (e.g., invoices, order confirmations) are communicated via mediums like print, email, or EDI. Key transactions (NACE, VV11) and tables (NAST, TNAPR) are provided.

5. **Material Determination**: Facilitates material substitution for various reasons, such as promotions or availability. Key transactions (VB11, VB12) and tables (KONH, KONP) are included.

6. **Master Data Interdependencies**: Explores the relationships between Customer Master Data, Material Master Data, and Organizational Data in creating sales orders and quotations. It highlights the role of pricing, output determination, and material validation in the I2O process.

The presentation also includes a version history, branding elements (Rexroth, A Bosch Company), and a Q&A section. The futuristic design and 'Grownfield' concept emphasize the integration of People, Process, and Technology in a connected system. Changes in Process: Subcontracting Process with MRP-Area
Enhancements in the subcontracting process from SAP ERP release 4.0 logic to 4.5 logic in S/4HANA.
A BOM (Bill of Materials) is needed to list the components which should be sent to the supplier.
A production version with a reference to the BOM is required. A reference to routing is not necessary.
An MRP area for each subcontractor must be created, with specific planning parameters (such as MRP type, lot sizing, procurement type) selectable for materials at the subcontracting MRP area level.
Default planning parameters are used if MRP area-specific material master records do not exist.
Separates subcontracting demand and stock into single subcontracting planning segments. Uncovered subcontracting demand is planned together with internal demand in the make-to-stock planning segment.
Plans the demand for each subcontractor separately using subcontracting MRP areas (available from SAP ERP release 4.5 logic).
Links provided to the Purchasing Subcontracting Process in S4.
generated_answer: Single-level planning runs in MRP focus on the immediate requirements for a specific material, considering only the direct demand and inventory levels for that material. In contrast, multi-level planning runs take into account the entire bill of materials (BOM) structure, assessing the requirements for all components needed to produce a finished product, thereby considering both direct and indirect demands across multiple levels of the product hierarchy.

Material Master Data Report - FIORI User Documentation
This document provides guidance on analyzing controlling-relevant master data fields as part of the L3(V) process 'Perform Cost Object Reporting'. It focuses on the use of a FIORI App for this purpose.
The material master is a critical component in the product costing process. To facilitate the analysis of material master data in bulk, a FIORI App has been developed. This app allows users to efficiently check and analyze material master data fields in mass.
The FIORI Launchpad provides access to all relevant reporting apps under costing accounting. The Material Master Extraction app enables users to display material master data fields in bulk.
The header color in the app indicates the source table of each field. Controlling-relevant fields primarily originate from the MARA, MARC, and MBEW tables.
Users can customize the layout using the provided symbol. Additional relevant fields can be added from the following tables: MARA, MARC, MBEW, MLGN, MARD, MVKE, and MDMA.

This document provides guidance on analyzing controlling-relevant master data fields as part of the L3(V) process 'Perform Cost Object Reporting'. It focuses on the use of a FIORI App for this purpose.
The material master is a critical component in the product costing process. To facilitate the analysis of material master data in bulk, a FIORI App has been developed. This app allows users to efficiently check and analyze material master data fields in mass.
The FIORI Launchpad provides access to all relevant reporting apps under costing accounting. The Material Master Extraction app enables users to display material master data fields in bulk.
The header color in the app indicates the source table of each field. Controlling-relevant fields primarily originate from the MARA, MARC, and MBEW tables.
Users can customize the layout using the provided symbol. Additional relevant fields can be added from the following tables: MARA, MARC, MBEW, MLGN, MARD, MVKE, and MDMA.

1. Open transaction **QA01**.

A Quality Info Record (Q-Info Record) is a document that captures information about the relationship between a material and a supplier, particularly when a quality assurance agreement or supplier approval is necessary. Q-Info Records ensure quality control in procurement by helping block suppliers who consistently provide defective materials.

A quality certificate can be recorded and managed in procurement by following these steps:

1. **Purchase Order Creation**: The buyer creates a purchase order, which initiates the procurement process.

2. **Goods Receipt Posting**: Upon receiving the delivery, the Warehouse Clerk posts the goods receipt for the purchase order item.

3. **Inspection Lot Generation**: The system automatically generates an inspection lot when the goods receipt is posted.

4. **Quality Certificate Evaluation**: Check if the supplier has included the required quality certificate with the shipment.

5. **Status Update**:
   - If the certificate is confirmed, proceed to post the usage decision, allowing the transfer of items from quality inspection to unrestricted use stock.
   - If the certificate is missing, confirm the receipt of the certificate from the supplier, updating the inspection lot status to CTCM (Certificate Missing).

6. **Documentation Confirmation**: Document and confirm the receipt of the quality certificate in the system before executing the usage decision.

7. **Usage Decision**: Once the certificate is confirmed, the system allows the transfer of items to unrestricted use, ensuring compliance with quality standards.

The process is governed by settings in the material master, specifically the QM control key (YV05) and certificate type (YV01), which mandate the receipt of the quality certificate for a usage decision to be executed.

question: What are the steps to manually convert a planned order into a production order using MD04?
golden_answer: To manually convert a planned order into a production order using MD04: 1) Open transaction MD04 and select the relevant planned order from the list. 2) Double-click the planned order to open it. 3) In the popup window, click the 'Prod.Ord.' button, which redirects to transaction CO40. 4) Execute the material availability check and click 'Save' to create the production order with the system status set to CRTD (Created).

question: How can missing parts impact the release of a production order, and how is this managed?
golden_answer: Missing parts prevent the release of a production order, resulting in the system status MSPT (Missing Parts). In this case, the production order can be saved without release, and missing parts management is performed until all materials are available. Once resolved, the production order can be released with the status updated to REL (Released).

To apply the concept of 'Make to Order' (MTO) in managing production and supply for customer-specific demands, follow these steps:

1. **Sales Order Creation**: Initiate the process by creating a sales order that specifies the customer's requirements for the product.

2. **Material Master Configuration**: Ensure that the material master settings are configured to support MTO, including defining the strategy group and requirement class.

3. **Material Requirements Planning (MRP)**: Run MRP to generate Planned Orders (PldOrd) based on the sales order demand, balancing it against available inventory.

4. **Planned Order Conversion**: Convert the planned orders into production orders, ensuring that they are linked to the specific sales order items for traceability.

5. **Production Order Release**: Release the production orders using appropriate SAP transactions (e.g., MD04 for manual release or COHV for mass processing).

6. **Material Supply Management**: Automatically create material supply and warehouse requests upon production order release to ensure that all necessary components are available.

7. **Production Execution**: Confirm operations through the system, updating statuses as production progresses (e.g., from Created to Released, and then to Confirmed).

8. **Goods Delivery**: Upon completion of production, post the goods receipt, linking the finished products to the sales order for accurate tracking and inventory management.

9. **Cost Tracking**: Collect costs associated with the production orders to analyze profit margins and ensure accurate financial reporting.

10. **Customer Communication**: Maintain communication with the customer throughout the process to ensure satisfaction with the customization and delivery timelines.

By following these steps, MTO can effectively manage production and supply tailored to individual customer demands, enhancing customization, reducing inventory costs, and improving customer satisfaction.

Comprehensive Overview of Quality Management (QM) Processes and Product Compliance in SAP S/4HANA
This comprehensive guide provides an in-depth overview of Quality Management (QM) processes and Product Compliance within the SAP S/4HANA environment, tailored for roles such as Quality Managers, Problem Coordinators, and QM Key Users. The training emphasizes the transition from SAP R/3 to S/4HANA, the integration of Extended Warehouse Management (EWM), and the strategic shift from 'Quality' to 'Excellence.'

Key Highlights:

1. **QM Process Overview:**
   - Introduction to the 'Grownfield' theme, focusing on People, Technology, and Process.
   - Learning objectives include understanding QM processes in Country Unit (CU) templates, identifying changes from R/3 to S/4HANA, and mastering display transactions and master data management.

2. **Process Changes (SAP R/3 to S/4HANA):**
   - Updates in Goods Receipt Inspection, Supplier Notifications, and Customer Complaints.
   - Introduction of new notification types (ZT, ZC, ZL) and changes in inspection origins and task management.

3. **Future Process and Innovation:**
   - Transitioning from 'Quality' to 'Excellence' with a focus on innovation and integration.
   - Visual representations of interconnected elements under the 'Grownfield' theme.

4. **Quality Master Data Management:**
   - Detailed instructions for managing Material Master QM View, Quality Info Records (Q-Info), Dynamic Modification Rules (DMR), Sampling Procedures, Production Resources Tools (PRT), and Master Inspection Characteristics (MIC) using SAP transaction codes (e.g., MM03, QI03, QDR3, QDV3, CF02, QS24, CRQ3).

5. **Extended Warehouse Management (EWM):**
   - Overview of EWM as a modern, flexible warehouse management system integrated with S/4HANA.
   - Key elements include handling units, storage types, storage bins, and warehouse numbers.
   - Processes for stock management, goods receipt, and using the Warehouse Management Monitor (/SCWM/MON).

6. **Inspection and Complaint Processes:**
   - Goods Receipt Inspection: Standardized processes for inspecting supplier parts, creating inspection lots, recording results, and making usage decisions (T-codes: QA32, QA33, QA03, QE51N, QA11/QA12, QA13).
   - Supplier Complaints: Use of Quality Notification Type Y2 for documenting supplier errors during goods receipt, production, or service (T-codes: QM01, QM03, QM11).
   - Ad-hoc Inspections: Addressing unexpected quality issues or supplier concerns through blocking parts, creating inspection lots, and making usage decisions.
   - Customer Complaints: Handling technical (ZT), commercial (ZC), and logistics (ZL) complaints with detailed notification processes and Fiori app support (e.g., QM10, QM11, QM12, QM14).

7. **Product Compliance:**
   - Ensures adherence to RB/GF 182 standards by verifying product compliance with jurisdictional requirements during sales document creation.
   - Compliance checks are automated using background tables (POSLI, NEGLI_PH, NEGLI), with errors triggering communication between product and sales teams.
   - Target country determination prioritizes the end customer's country over the ship-to party's country.

8. **Exercises and Support:**
   - Users are encouraged to practice display transactions and processes as demonstrated in the module.
   - Support is available through designated contacts, such as Patil Nitin Gyandev (DC/QMM).

This guide emphasizes the importance of leveraging SAP S/4HANA functionalities to streamline quality management, enhance operational visibility, and ensure compliance, aligning with Bosch Rexroth AG's vision of 'Quality to Excellence.'

question: What are the key differences between SAP R/3 and SAP S/4 in terms of the QM-View and Quality Management processes?
golden_answer: In SAP R/3, the Q-Module was used in most plants and sporadically in country units, while in SAP S/4 it is used in all plants and country units. Material Master Data (QM-View) in SAP R/3 had plant or country-specific settings, whereas SAP S/4 standardizes the settings for all goods receipts (excluding indirect materials). Additionally, the automatic creation of QM-View via BRF+ was limited to some country units in SAP R/3 but is implemented in all plants and country units in SAP S/4.

question: How can the release quantity feature in a Quality Info Record be used to control procurement activities?
golden_answer: The release quantity feature in a Quality Info Record allows setting a maximum ordered quantity for a material-supplier combination. The system accumulates the total ordered quantities, and once the specified limit is reached, no further purchase orders are permitted for that combination, thus controlling procurement activities.

question: What are the key differences between Quality Info Records in SAP R/3 and SAP S/4HANA?
golden_answer: In SAP R/3, the Q-Module was used in most plants and sporadically in country units, whereas in SAP S/4HANA, it is expanded to all plants and country units. Q-Info Record settings in SAP S/4HANA are standardized across all goods receipts (excluding indirect materials). The status profile in SAP R/3, which controlled goods receipt inspections, is replaced in SAP S/4HANA by the Production Part Approval Status, which describes the status of the production part approval process.

Key differences between Quality Info Records in SAP R/3 and SAP S/4HANA include:

1. **Use of the Q-Module**: In SAP R/3, the Q-Module was used in most plants and sporadically in country units, whereas in SAP S/4HANA, it is utilized in all plants and country units.

2. **Q-Info Record Settings**: SAP R/3 had plant or country unit-specific settings for Q-Info Records, while SAP S/4HANA has standardized Q-Info Record settings for all goods receipts, excluding indirect materials.

3. **Status Profile**: In SAP R/3, a status schema could be specified for the release, but in SAP S/4HANA, the status of the Q-Info Record controls the goods receipt inspection for both initial samples and series production. The status profile feature is no longer available due to the integration with Extended Warehouse Management (EWM).

4. **Production Part Approval Status**: This feature did not exist in SAP R/3 but is present in SAP S/4HANA, describing the status of the production part approval process and serving as an alternative for the status profile.

question: What is the purpose of ZT-type Quality Notifications in the Technical Customer Complaints process?
golden_answer: The purpose of ZT-type Quality Notifications is to handle warranty-related service requests and quality issues by documenting investigation results, managing complaints, and ensuring all relevant data for reporting is maintained in one object. They replace the Y3-type CS Notifications from the R/3 system in the S/4HANA system.

question: What are the steps to create a Quality Notification within a Service Request using the Fiori app?
golden_answer: To create a Quality Notification within a Service Request using the Fiori app, the user must first open the Service Request in edit mode by clicking 'Edit' at the top beside the Service Request title. Then, click on the three dots at the top-right corner of the interface and select 'Create Quality Notification.' A pop-up will appear at the bottom of the screen; click 'Save' to create the Quality Notification. The Quality Notification will be linked to the Service Request, and the necessary data will be automatically transferred.

question: What are the differences between ZC and ZL Quality Notifications in the SAP S/4HANA system?
golden_source: Q2E-02.060 Sales Logistics Customer Complaint FIORI.pptx
golden_answer: ZC-type Quality Notifications are used for sales/commercial errors, such as sold wrong product/model code or discrepancies in customer purchase orders. ZL-type Quality Notifications are used for logistics complaints, such as wrong product delivery, damaged goods, or shipment errors. ZC is created for sales-related issues, while ZL is created for logistics-related issues.

Technical Customer Complaints Process and Quality Notifications Guide
This comprehensive guide provides an in-depth overview of the Technical Customer Complaints process within Bosch Rexroth's S/4HANA system, focusing on the transition from the legacy R/3 system to S/4HANA. The process is designed to handle warranty-related service requests and quality issues through the creation and management of ZT-type Quality Notifications. Key aspects include:

1. **Process Overview**: The legacy Y3-type CS Notifications in R/3 have been replaced by ZT-type Quality Notifications in S/4HANA. The process begins with creating a Service Request, followed by generating a Quality Notification for warranty cases. The transition emphasizes streamlined processes, enhanced integration, and a focus on 'Quality to Excellence' under the GROWNFIELD initiative.

2. **Roles and Responsibilities**: Service Agents, Blue Collar Workers, Problem Coordinators, Quality Engineers, and Quality Managers collaborate to manage and investigate customer complaints, maintain notifications, and coordinate follow-up activities.

3. **Key Functionalities**:

question: What are the key changes in the Quality Management processes when transitioning from SAP R/3 to S/4HANA?
golden_answer: Key changes include the inspection origin for Goods Receipt Inspection changing to Origin 17 due to integration with Extended Warehouse Management (EWM), partial usage decisions for Goods Receipt Inspection lots being conducted at the Handling Unit (HU) level, and the replacement of CS notification type Y3 with ZT for Customer Technical Complaints. Additionally, YR type logistic notifications were replaced with ZC for Customer Commercial complaints and ZL for Customer Logistic complaints.

   - Introduction to the 'Grownfield' theme, focusing on People, Technology, and Process.
   - Learning objectives include understanding QM processes in Country Unit (CU) templates, identifying changes from R/3 to S/4HANA, and mastering display transactions and master data management.

2. **Process Changes (SAP R/3 to S/4HANA):**
   - Updates in Goods Receipt Inspection, Supplier Notifications, and Customer Complaints.
   - Introduction of new notification types (ZT, ZC, ZL) and changes in inspection origins and task management.

3. **Future Process and Innovation:**
   - Transitioning from 'Quality' to 'Excellence' with a focus on innovation and integration.
   - Visual representations of interconnected elements under the 'Grownfield' theme.

4. **Quality Master Data Management:**
   - Detailed instructions for managing Material Master QM View, Quality Info Records (Q-Info), Dynamic Modification Rules (DMR), Sampling Procedures, Production Resources Tools (PRT), and Master Inspection Characteristics (MIC) using SAP transaction codes (e.g., MM03, QI03, QDR3, QDV3, CF02, QS24, CRQ3).

5. **Extended Warehouse Management (EWM):**
   - Overview of EWM as a modern, flexible warehouse management system integrated with S/4HANA.
   - Key elements include handling units, storage types, storage bins, and warehouse numbers.
   - Processes for stock management, goods receipt, and using the Warehouse Management Monitor (/SCWM/MON).

6. **Inspection and Complaint Processes:**
   - Goods Receipt Inspection: Standardized processes for inspecting supplier parts, creating inspection lots, recording results, and making usage decisions (T-codes: QA32, QA33, QA03, QE51N, QA11/QA12, QA13).
   - Supplier Complaints: Use of Quality Notification Type Y2 for documenting supplier errors during goods receipt, production, or service (T-codes: QM01, QM03, QM11).
   - Ad-hoc Inspections: Addressing unexpected quality issues or supplier concerns through blocking parts, creating inspection lots, and making usage decisions.
   - Customer Complaints: Handling technical (ZT), commercial (ZC), and logistics (ZL) complaints with detailed notification processes and Fiori app support (e.g., QM10, QM11, QM12, QM14).

7. **Product Compliance:**
   - Ensures adherence to RB/GF 182 standards by verifying product compliance with jurisdictional requirements during sales document creation.
   - Compliance checks are automated using background tables (POSLI, NEGLI_PH, NEGLI), with errors triggering communication between product and sales teams.
   - Target country determination prioritizes the end customer's country over the ship-to party's country.

8. **Exercises and Support:**
   - Users are encouraged to practice display transactions and processes as demonstrated in the module.
   - Support is available through designated contacts, such as Patil Nitin Gyandev (DC/QMM).

The Goods Receipt Inspection process ensures product quality and compliance through several key steps:

1. **Quality Checks**: Incoming goods are inspected for defects, damages, or deviations from established quality standards. This proactive approach helps identify issues before products enter inventory.

2. **Conformity Verification**: The process verifies that goods comply with technical and legal requirements, ensuring that all products meet necessary regulations and standards.

3. **Documentation Review**: Accompanying documents are reviewed to ensure they align with purchase orders and quality requirements. This step prevents discrepancies and ensures that all necessary documentation is in place.

4. **Standardized Processes**: The use of standardized Material Master Data (Q-View), Q-Info records, and inspection plans ensures consistency in how goods are handled and inspected.

5. **Dynamic Modification Rules**: The implementation of dynamic modification rules allows for flexibility in the inspection process, adapting to different types of goods and inspection requirements.

6. **Usage Decision**: Based on inspection results, a usage decision is made to either accept or reject the goods, ensuring that only compliant products are accepted into inventory.

By following these steps, the Goods Receipt Inspection process helps maintain high product quality, reduces the risk of errors, and enhances customer satisfaction.

Introduction: 2.3. Main Topics | Process Overview
In SAP, an inspection plan defines the specific procedures and characteristics to be inspected for a material or group of materials. It outlines the sequence of inspection operations, the characteristics to be checked, and the required test equipment. Inspection plans are used for various purposes, such as goods receipt, goods issue, and recurring inspections.
Inspection plans help to ensure that materials meet the required quality standards.
They provide a standardized approach to inspection, reducing variability and improving consistency.
By defining the inspection process, they streamline the inspection workflow and minimize time and effort.
Inspection plans enable the tracking of inspection results and the analysis of quality trends.

The key components of the Q2E inspection plan process include:

1. **Purchase Order or Scheduling Agreement**: Initiates the process for a material.
2. **Goods Receipt (GR)**: Upon receiving goods, if configured for inspection, an inspection lot is automatically created by SAP.
3. **Inspection Plan Determination**: SAP identifies the appropriate inspection plan using a predefined hierarchy, starting with the QM Info Record, followed by material-specific and general plans.
4. **Inspection Execution**: Quality inspectors record results based on the characteristics outlined in the inspection plan.
5. **Usage Decision (UD)**: Based on inspection results, a decision is made (e.g., "Accept" or "Reject"), which influences stock postings.

These components are managed through the SAP S/4HANA system, utilizing the QM view in master data, quality info records, and inspection plans to ensure materials meet quality standards and streamline the inspection workflow.

4.1.4. Basic Data: MIC – Master Inspection Characteristic
▪Master inspection characteristics greatly simplify work in the context of inspection planning. A master inspection
characteristic is an inspection characteristic created as a master record that is intended for frequent use in
inspection plans and should be able to be evaluated across inspection plans. Once a master inspection
characteristic has been created, it can be integrated into an inspection plan with little effort and in various ways
▪There is a further advantage in results recording: under certain circumstances, it may be necessary to record
results for another, unplanned characteristic in addition to the characteristics defined in the inspection
plan. This is only possible, however, with the help of master inspection characteristics.
▪There are 3 different options for this (which you define yourself in the master inspection characteristic):
▪
Referenced characteristic: Referencing master inspection characteristics means that a change to the master inspection
characteristic is automatically reflected in all inspection plans in which this characteristic was referenced. The characteristic
appears in the inspection plan as a coupled characteristic (recognizable by the link symbol
). It is then not possible to make
changes to the inspection characteristic in the inspection plan itself (the fields are grayed out). However, it is possible to
remove the referencing. The master inspection characteristic then only has the function of a copy template.
▪
Complete master copy: All data for the inspection characteristic is maintained here and can be transferred 1:1 to the
inspection plan. Example: It was determined for a quantitative master inspection characteristic that an upper and lower limit
value is to be maintained for this. You have the option of entering the associated numbers in the master inspection
characteristic. These can then be adopted immediately in the inspection plan. However, it is also possible to overwrite them.
▪
Incomplete master copy: In contrast to this, these values can be left open for the incomplete master copy. They must then be
entered in the inspection plan.

question: How can accurate billing be ensured in a Fieldservice scenario where a technician records working hours, materials used, and travel costs?

It emphasizes the use of SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM) and SAP S/4HANA for efficient production supply and outbound operations.

**Key Highlights:**
1. **Overview:**
   - Introduction to SAP EWM tools for managing storage and material staging.
   - Preferred method for production supply is the Production Material Request (PMR), which ensures precise quantity allocation, stock reservation, and real-time updates.
   - Basic master data setup includes defining Production Supply Areas (PSA), control cycles, staging methods, and production scheduling profiles.

2. **Material Staging and Picking:**
   - Detailed instructions for checking PMR status using transactions like /SCWM/Mon and /SCWM/Stage.
   - Steps for creating and confirming warehouse tasks (WTs) for material picking using RF applications.
   - Visual aids include screenshots of SAP interfaces and examples of pick lists with warehouse order details.

3. **Consumption:**
   - Consumption is triggered via SAP transaction MIGO by posting goods issues for production orders.
   - Instructions include marking items, navigating through components, and posting movements to create material documents with 261 movements.
   - Monitoring tools like /SCWM/Mon and MB51 are used to track consumption and movement details.

4. **Reversal Process:**
   - Reversal of PMR steps is possible through SAP GUI or Fiori apps, including cancellation, return delivery, and partial/full quantity reversals.
   - Methods include using transactions like /SCWM/Mon, /SCWM/ADPROD, and /SCWM/PACK, or the Fiori app 'Clear Production Supply Area.'
   - Visual content includes screenshots of SAP interfaces for material selection, warehouse task creation, and confirmation.

**Visual and Branding Elements:**

Process Overview: Good to Know | Definition
To ensure material availability during service execution, required parts can be added directly to a Service Order—whether for Field Service or Inhouse Repair. This is the prerequisite to start the Purchase process, resulting in a Purchase Order that reserves and tracks the needed items. All related transactions can be viewed in the Transaction History.
A technician is scheduled to repair a device at a customer site. Before dispatch, the planner adds the necessary spare parts to the Service Order. Meanwhile, in another case, a device sent in for inhouse repair requires additional components. If the required materials are not available in stock, they are automatically flagged for procurement. This triggers the purchasing process to ensure timely delivery of the needed parts—enabling smooth service execution in both field and inhouse scenarios.

question: What are the steps to create a service order in the R2S process?
golden_answer: To create a service order in the R2S process: 1) Navigate to the 'Items' section and add a template from In-house Repair or manually add relevant positions. 2) Click 'Edit' and then 'Actions'. 3) Select 'Receive Repair Object from Customer or any partner'.

question: Can you summarize the key steps involved in the R2S-02.120 NSGS/BBX process, from creating a service request to releasing for billing?

question: What is the purpose of the 'Release Billing' step in the R2S process?
golden_answer: The 'Release Billing' step marks the financial handover point at the end of the Inhouse Repair and Field Service processes. It triggers the creation of billing documents and ensures that all performed services or repairs can be invoiced correctly.

flagged for procurement. This triggers the purchasing process to ensure timely delivery of the needed parts 
– enabling smooth service execution in both field and inhouse scenarios.

golden_answer: To create a service order using the Fiori app: 1) Open the 'Create Service Order' app or use the follow-up button in the contract. 2) Select the transaction type (e.g., FS Order YV02 for field service or Rep.Order YV01 for in-house repair). 3) Enter details such as description, sold-to party ID, contact person, account indicator (chargeable), and product ID. 4) Classify the request using Category fields. 5) Enter organizational data such as service and sales organizational units. 6) Verify the 'Parties Involved' tab and save the service order. 7) Edit the 'Items' tab to add a bundle item product ID and quantity. 8) Select the appropriate contract from the fetched list. 9) Add a service item under the 'Items' tab, input the service item ID and quantity, and save to generate the service order number.

It acts as the formal closure of service activities and is mandatory for following processes like customer invoicing or outbound delivery.

question: How does the transition from R/3 to S/4 systems impact transaction codes in the Purchasing Data Cockpit?
golden_source: S2C-00.010 Purchasing Data Cockpit (Training DCPL) - slides.pptx
golden_answer: The transition from R/3 to S/4 systems involves mapping old transaction codes to new ones in S/4. For example, the R/3 transaction '/RB9S/PROC_PDC' for the Entry Page is replaced with '/RB4R/MM_PDC' in S/4, and similar mappings exist for Info Records, Source Lists, Scheduling Agreements, and Quota Arrangements.

This presentation, titled 'O2C-02.010 Manage Sales Order Standard,' provides a detailed guide to the standard sales order process within the 'Order to Cash' (O2C) framework, focusing on the transition from SAP R/3 to SAP S/4 systems. The learning targets emphasize understanding and optimizing the sales order process, highlighting key differences between SAP S/4 and R/3 systems. The introduction outlines affected business roles, the Signavio Process Documentation, and the main topics, including creating standard sales orders (YVC1) with or without references, using transaction VA01.

The 'Changes in Process' section focuses on the transition from SAP R/3 to S/4, highlighting key differences in the systems. The 'Future Process' section provides a step-by-step guide to the standard sales order process in SAP S/4, including creating orders, setting organizational data, selecting references, maintaining header data, entering material numbers, executing pricing, saving orders, managing message output, and attaching business documents. Each step is accompanied by detailed instructions, visual aids, and examples.

The presentation also includes an exercise for creating a standard sales order using SAP VA01, with step-by-step instructions and visual illustrations. The 'Attachments' section provides useful links to resources such as the Signavio Process Collaboration Hub and Docupedia for further learning.

The presentation concludes with a 'Thank You' slide, encouraging feedback, and a 'Version History' slide that documents the evolution of the standard sales order process presentation. The design features sleek, abstract digital themes with interconnected elements representing people, technology, and processes under the 'Grownfield' initiative.

The key changes in the purchasing organization structure from SAP R/3 to SAP S/4 include:

1. **Direct and Indirect Purchasing Codes**: The organizational codes for direct and indirect purchasing have been updated. For example, in SAP R/3, direct purchasing used codes like PR1, PRA, and PRP, while in SAP S/4, the corresponding codes are DCPU and DCPB for direct purchasing.

2. **Intercompany and Indirect Procurement**: The codes for intercompany transactions and indirect procurement have also changed, with new identifiers introduced in S/4.

3. **Enhanced Data Visibility**: SAP S/4 provides a more detailed and organized view of purchasing area data, improving clarity and accessibility compared to R/3.

4. **Partner Roles Maintenance**: In S/4, partner roles for external vendors are maintained through PMD Lookup and Athena, whereas in R/3, they were managed directly in the system.

5. **Plant Extension Requirements**: The requirement for plant extensions has been modified, necessitating a plant view only if specific values differ from the purchasing organization level.

These changes reflect a modernization and optimization of the procurement processes in SAP S/4.

This presentation, titled 'O2C-02.010 Manage Sales Order Standard,' provides a detailed guide to the standard sales order process within the 'Order to Cash' (O2C) framework, focusing on the transition from SAP R/3 to SAP S/4 systems. It is branded under 'Rexroth | A Bosch Company' and incorporates the 'Grownfield' initiative, which emphasizes the integration of people, technology, and processes.

The agenda includes sections on learning targets, an introduction to the process, changes in the workflow, the future process, and attachments. The learning targets emphasize understanding and optimizing the sales order process, highlighting key differences between SAP S/4 and R/3 systems. The introduction outlines affected business roles, the Signavio Process Documentation, and the main topics, including creating standard sales orders (YVC1) with or without references, using transaction VA01.

The 'Changes in Process' section focuses on the transition from SAP R/3 to S/4, highlighting key differences in the systems. The 'Future Process' section provides a step-by-step guide to the standard sales order process in SAP S/4, including creating orders, setting organizational data, selecting references, maintaining header data, entering material numbers, executing pricing, saving orders, managing message output, and attaching business documents. Each step is accompanied by detailed instructions, visual aids, and examples.

question: How does the SAP EWM system ensure accurate stock data when discrepancies occur between ERP and EWM stock levels?
golden_answer: The SAP EWM system uses the /SCWM/ERP_STOCKCHECK report to compare stock levels between ERP and EWM. When discrepancies occur, the system assumes the EWM stock data is correct and adjusts the ERP stock accordingly, ensuring no stock discrepancies and clearing any hanging queues.

Process Overview | 1.1 Good to know | Definition
SAP S/4HANA provides a comprehensive Service Contract Management capability enabling long-term service agreements with customers. These contracts cover fixed recurring fees, entitlements, billing automation, renewals, and integration with service execution. Service contract management handles two business cases: 1) Billing of recurring fixed fees under the contract, and 2) Service orders for extra activities, spare parts, travel, or consumption that are outside the contracted scope.
Fixed Recurring Services
Customers can avail regular recurring services against a fixed period rate contract. Billing is handled via contract documents as per the predefined billing plan. Costs are settled to the contract item.
Additional Services
Customers can be billed for additional services not included in the fixed fee contract. Billing is done using service orders instead of the contract billing plan. However, the costs and revenues are settled to the contract item.

Exchange Handling Process Overview
The Exchange Handling process within the R2S (Request to Service) framework is a structured workflow designed to manage the replacement of defective components with exchange parts using SAP S/4HANA. The process ensures full traceability of material movements, costs, and billing activities by effectively linking Service Requests, Service Orders, and Sales Orders. The workflow includes creating a service request, generating service and sales orders, posting goods receipts, creating internal orders, forwarding materials to repair centers, and finalizing service orders. Key steps include:

1. Creating a Service Request via the Fiori App and categorizing it as 'Exchange.'
2. Generating a Service Order using the Follow-Up functionality and selecting the appropriate transaction type.
3. Adding a Service Order Template to the item section of the order.
4. Creating a Sales Order via VA01 or the Fiori App, entering organizational and exchange-specific data.
5. Linking the Sales Order to the transaction history using the 'Subsequent Assignment' function.
6. Posting the goods receipt for the defective part upon arrival at the responsible country unit.
7. Creating an internal order as a cost collector and setting the status to 'Plan Repair.'
8. Forwarding the material to the repair center by entering the 'Ship-To Party/Repair Center' in the 'Parties involved' tab and using the 'Forward Repair Object to Repair Center' action.
9. Finalizing the Service Order by entering the repair center's result report, confirming labor times, performing optional billing, and setting the status to 'Completed.'

Guide to Packing Goods for Outbound Shipping in SAP EWM
This guide provides an overview of the process for packing goods for outbound shipping using SAP Extended Warehouse Management (EWM). The process begins by accessing the transaction `scwm.pack` and selecting the warehouse number and outbound delivery order in the warehouse request field. The packer typically receives a picking list and manually checks for any order-related packing information, as there are no automatic flags or pop-ups for such details. Delivery items are packed into shipping handling units (HUs) by selecting the material, choosing appropriate packaging material, and using drag-and-drop functionality. The system can automatically pre-fill the new handling unit, and the packer can adjust the weight, volume, and dimensions as needed. Once packed, the handling unit label is printed, and the process is finalized in the packing monitor. This triggers background activities such as determining the forwarder, updating the ERP outbound delivery, and preparing the goods for physical movement to the staging area. The process may vary depending on the warehouse structure and organization.
